definition_zh: 有节奏的；抑扬顿挫的；（占星）落陷的
definition_en: having rhythm or a falling cadence; in astrology, falling or placed in a cadent house
core_image: 鼓点一起一落，脚步随节拍起伏
scene: 雨点敲着屋檐，像一支不慌不忙的鼓。 The rain fell in cadent beats against the eaves.
sceneCN: 这里 cadent 是「有节奏的、一起一落的」（第 1 个义项：随节拍落下的）；句意是雨点有节奏地敲打屋檐。

senses.title: Moving with rhythm or cadence
senses.definition: falling or moving with a measured, rhythmic beat
senses.definitionCN: 随有节拍的律动一起一落
senses.example: The oars kept a cadent splash through the calm water.
senses.exampleCN: 船桨在平静的水面划出有节奏的水声。
senses.why: The Latin present participle of cadere means falling, and rhythm is a measured falling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cadere 的现在分词意为「落下」，节奏正是有规律的落下。

senses.title: Falling in astrology
senses.definition: in traditional astrology, placed in a cadent house, away from the chart's angles
senses.definitionCN: 传统占星学中指行星位于果宫、远离四正宫位
senses.example: In the old chart, Mars was cadent and weak.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧星盘上，火星落陷而力弱。
senses.why: The falling sense was taken literally by astrologers for planets away from power.
senses.whyCN: 占星家取「落下」的字面义，指行星远离强势宫位。

intro.en: Cadent is the Latin present participle cadens of cadere, to fall, taken straight into English.
intro.cn: cadent 是拉丁语 cadere（落下）的现在分词 cadens，直接进入英语。

items.en: a reconstructed root kad- for falling stands behind the Latin verb; details remain debated.
items.cn: 拉丁动词背后是表示「落下」的重构词根 kad-，细节尚存争议。

items.en: cadere meant to fall; cadens meant falling.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为「落下」，cadens 意为「正落下的」。

items.en: in astrological Latin, cadens described planets in weak houses.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中，占星家用 cadens 描述弱势宫位中的行星。

items.en: English borrowed cadent chiefly in the astrological sense.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语借入 cadent，主要用于占星义。

items.en: the rhythmic sense survives in literary use alongside cadence.
items.cn: 如今节奏义在文学语域与 cadence 并存。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the falling root; the near-meaning group gathers rhythm words.
note.cn: 形近组同出「落下」词根；近义组是节奏类词。

definition_zh: 蒸散；蒸发蒸腾；地表水分经土壤蒸发与植物蒸腾共同进入大气的过程
definition_en: the combined transfer of water from the land surface to the atmosphere through evaporation from soil and open water and through transpiration from plants
core_image: 烈日下的农田向上吐出水汽：土面在蒸发，叶孔在蒸腾，两股看不见的水汽合为一股上升流
scene: 干旱区的试验田里，测量仪昼夜记录土面蒸发与作物叶片失水合成的总量。 The lysimeter recorded evapotranspiration from the irrigated field around the clock.
sceneCN: 这里 evapotranspiration 指「地表水分经土壤蒸发与植物蒸腾共同进入大气的总量」（第 1 个义项：蒸发与蒸腾两条通道合成的水分输出）；句意为蒸渗仪昼夜不停记录这块灌溉田的蒸散量。图中可辨识物件：试验田、蒸渗仪、土面、作物叶片。

pos.zh: 蒸散；蒸发蒸腾（不可数，水文学与农学计量名词）

forms.label: 计量复数（不同地块的蒸散量）

derivatives.zh: 蒸散（技术文献中的罕见动词）

senses.title: The combined water loss from land to air
senses.titleCN: 地表向大气的水分总输出
senses.definition: the total flux of water from soil, open water and plant leaves into the atmosphere, counted as one process
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、自由水面与植物叶片进入大气的水分总通量，作为一个过程来计算
senses.example: The lysimeter recorded evapotranspiration from the irrigated field around the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸渗仪昼夜不停记录这块灌溉田的蒸散量。
senses.why: The word is a deliberate blend of evaporation and transpiration, because hydrologists needed one label for two channels that leave the ground together and cannot be separated in the field.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是有意把 evaporation 与 transpiration 合在一起，因为水文学家需要一个名称来指两条同时离开地面、在野外无法分开的通道。

senses.title: The plant-only share of the flux
senses.titleCN: 其中由植物蒸腾贡献的部分
senses.definition: the portion of the flux that passes through stomata of living plants rather than through bare soil
senses.definitionCN: 经由活体植物气孔而非裸露土面进入大气的那一部分通量
senses.example: A wheat canopy gave transpiration the larger share of evapotranspiration.
senses.exampleCN: 在麦田冠层中，蒸腾占了蒸散的较大份额。
senses.why: Once the compound was in use, its two halves could be pulled apart again, and this sense names the plant half alone.
senses.whyCN: 复合词一旦通用，它的两半又可以被重新分开，这个义项就单指植物那一半。

senses.title: A measured depth of water per unit time
senses.titleCN: 以水深与时间表示的观测量
senses.definition: the quantity expressed as millimetres of water lost per day or per season over a defined area
senses.definitionCN: 在给定面积上以每天或每季损失的水深毫米数表示的量
senses.example: The station reported an evapotranspiration of six millimetres a day.
senses.exampleCN: 该观测站报告的蒸散量为每天六毫米。
senses.why: Hydrology turns processes into numbers, so the same noun came to name the measured depth rather than only the physical event.
senses.whyCN: 水文学把过程变成数字，因此同一个名词也从物理事件转而指测量所得的水深。

senses.title: Crop water demand in irrigation planning
senses.titleCN: 灌溉计划中的作物需水量
senses.definition: the water a crop must receive to replace what it loses through evapotranspiration
senses.definitionCN: 为补足作物蒸散损失而必须供给的水量
senses.example: Irrigation was timed to match the crop evapotranspiration each week.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉按每周的作物蒸散量安排时间。
senses.why: In farm management the process becomes a demand to be met, since every millimetre lost must be replaced by rain or by the ditch.
senses.whyCN: 在农场管理中，这个过程变成必须满足的需求，因为每损失一毫米都得靠降雨或水渠补上。

senses.title: A term in the water-balance equation
senses.titleCN: 水量平衡方程中的输出项
senses.definition: the outflow term in a catchment water balance, set beside precipitation, runoff and storage change
senses.definitionCN: 流域水量平衡中的支出项，与降水、径流与蓄水量变化并列
senses.example: In the basin budget, evapotranspiration accounted for most of the rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 在流域水量收支中，蒸散占去了大部分降水。
senses.why: A budget must name every entry and exit; this sense fixes the word as the main exit in the accounting of a catchment.
senses.whyCN: 收支表必须给每一笔进出命名；这个义项把这个词固定为流域核算中的主要支出项。

senses.title: The latent-heat channel of the surface
senses.titleCN: 地表向大气的潜热通道
senses.definition: the same water flux viewed as latent heat that cools the surface and feeds the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 同一股水汽通量被看作潜热：它冷却地表并补给大气
senses.example: Satellites estimate evapotranspiration from the latent heat seen in thermal imagery.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星依据热红外影像中的潜热估算蒸散。
senses.why: Climate science reads the flux in energy units, because water leaving the surface carries heat away with it.
senses.whyCN: 气候学用能量单位读这股通量，因为离地的水把热量一并带走。

senses.title: Ecosystem water loss in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中的生态系统失水
senses.definition: the water an ecosystem returns to the air, which determines streamflow, soil moisture and carbon uptake
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统返回大气的水量，它决定径流、土壤湿度与碳吸收
senses.example: Deforestation lowered evapotranspiration and raised the dry-season flow.
senses.exampleCN: 砍伐森林降低了蒸散，抬高了旱季流量。
senses.why: Ecology stresses the consequence rather than the mechanism: what leaves the ecosystem is water no longer available to streams and roots.
senses.whyCN: 生态学强调的是后果而非机制：离开生态系统的水，就不再可供溪流与根系使用。

senses.title: Any slow invisible drain from a system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：系统里缓慢而不易察觉的流失
senses.definition: a gradual, unnoticed loss of a resource from a system, treated as if it were water rising away
senses.definitionCN: 资源从系统中缓慢、不易察觉地流失，被比作水汽升离地面
senses.example: The report described evapotranspiration of talent from the region.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把人才从该地区的外流描述为一种蒸散。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the physical shape: something valuable leaves quietly through many small openings, and the loss is noticed only in the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了物理形态：有价值之物经由许多小口悄然离去，直到看账本才发现少了。

intro.en: Evapotranspiration is a modern technical compound built from two older Latin-derived nouns, evaporation and transpiration. Each half has its own history; the compound itself is little more than a century old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: evapotranspiration 是近代技术复合词，由两个更古老的拉丁来源名词 evaporation 与 transpiration 合成。两半各有自己的历史，复合词本身仅有百余年。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vapor meant 'steam, exhalation, vapour'. Its deeper origin is not established; the suggestion that it imitates the sound of steam is a hypothesis, so any older Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: vapor 意为「蒸汽、呼出的气、雾汽」。其更深来源未得到证明；认为它模仿蒸汽之声的说法只是假说，因此凡为其给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

items.en: The prefix e- 'out' plus vaporare 'to emit vapour' gave evaporare 'to vapourize'; Medieval Latin evaporatio and English evaporation followed in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 前缀 e-「向外」加 vaporare「放出汽」构成 evaporare「使汽化」；中世纪拉丁 evaporatio 与英语 evaporation 随后在十七世纪出现。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe'. Its own origin is not settled; it is often placed beside a reconstructed root for blowing, but that form is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸」。它本身的来源没有定论；常被放在一个表示「吹」的重构词根旁，但那个形式是重构而非有书证的词。

items.en: Trans- 'through' plus spirare produced transpirare 'to breathe through, to let vapour pass out'; English transpiration first named the escape of vapour through plant surfaces.
items.cn: trans-「穿过」加 spirare 构成 transpirare「透过…呼吸、让汽透出」；英语 transpiration 最初指水汽经植物表面逸出。

items.en: Agricultural meteorology and hydrology joined the two nouns into one term for the combined flux, because field instruments cannot separate the soil and leaf channels.
items.cn: 农业气象学与水文学把两个名词合成一个术语，用来指合并后的通量，因为野外仪器无法把土面与叶片两条通道分开。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, and deeper origin of vapor and spirare): the compound entered print in the early twentieth century, but no single first citation is fixed, so the date is approximate; the roots behind vapor and spirare remain unsettled, and any forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，以及 vapor 与 spirare 的更深词源）：该复合词在二十世纪初进入印刷品，但没有公认的最早书证，年代只能约计；vapor 与 spirare 背后的词根仍无定论，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same vapour or breathing stock that are easily confused with the two halves of this term; group two holds other water-balance processes that are often mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「汽」或「呼吸」词干、容易与这个词的两半混淆的词；第二组是常被当作蒸散的其他水量平衡过程。

entries.definition: Loss of water as vapour from soil or open water without passing through a plant, so it names only one of the two channels.
entries.definitionCN: 水不经植物、直接从土面或自由水面化为水汽的损失，只指两条通道中的一条。

entries.definition: Water vapour leaving a plant through its stomata; standing alone it excludes direct evaporation from the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 水汽经植物气孔离开植物；单独使用时不含地面直接蒸发。

entries.definition: The physical change from liquid to vapour, a phase change rather than a land-surface flux.
entries.definitionCN: 由液态变为气态的物理变化，是相变而非地表通量。

entries.definition: Sweat, from Latin spirare through perspirare 'to breathe through'; it belongs to the same root but not to the water balance.
entries.definitionCN: 汗水，经拉丁 perspirare「透过呼吸」出自 spirare；与蒸散同根，但不属于水量平衡。

entries.definition: The water taken by a crop and not returned to the same basin; a planning term close to crop evapotranspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 作物取走且未回到同一流域的水量；是与作物蒸散接近的规划术语。

entries.definition: Direct change from snow or ice to vapour without melting; it bypasses the liquid stage that evaporation requires.
entries.definitionCN: 雪或冰不融化而直接变为水汽；它绕过了蒸发所需的液态阶段。

entries.definition: Change from vapour to liquid, the opposite direction of the same exchange between land and air.
entries.definitionCN: 由水汽变为液态，是陆地与大气之间同一交换的反方向。

entries.definition: Water that travels over the ground into streams; it is the other main exit from a catchment besides evapotranspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 沿地面流入溪流的水；是流域中除蒸散之外的另一主要支出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is evaporation plus transpiration, joined because instruments cannot split the two in the field.
normal.cn: 这个词就是 evaporation 加 transpiration，二者合称是因为野外仪器无法把它们分开。

normal.en: Vapor is 'steam'; spirare is 'to breathe'; trans- is 'through'.
normal.cn: vapor 是「蒸汽」；spirare 是「呼吸」；trans- 是「穿过」。

normal.en: The family runs evaporation, transpiration, vapor, vaporize and perspiration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evaporation、transpiration、vapor、vaporize 与 perspiration。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark measurement: actual, potential and reference evapotranspiration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出计量方式：实际蒸散量、潜在蒸散量、参考作物蒸散量。

normal.en: Hydrology writes it as ET, a term in the water balance beside precipitation and runoff.
normal.cn: 水文学把它写作 ET，是水量平衡中与降水、径流并列的项。

abstract.en: Picture two invisible plumes, one from bare soil and one from leaf pores, meeting above the field.
abstract.cn: 想象两股看不见的气流，一股来自裸露土面，一股来自叶孔，在田地上空汇合。

abstract.en: Picture a bank account drained by thousands of tiny unnoticeable withdrawals.
abstract.cn: 想象一个账户被成千上万笔难以察觉的小额支取慢慢掏空。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the heat itself escapes as the water leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，水离开的同时把热量也一并带走。

examples.en: Warm, dry air raises evapotranspiration across the whole basin.
examples.cn: 温暖干燥的空气抬高了整个流域的蒸散。

examples.en: The model separates evaporation from transpiration instead of treating evapotranspiration as one number.
examples.cn: 该模型把蒸发与蒸腾分开，而不是把蒸散当作一个数处理。

examples.en: Loss of vegetation reduced evapotranspiration and changed the regional rainfall pattern.
examples.cn: 植被减少降低了蒸散，改变了区域降水格局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）+ vapor（蒸汽）+ trans（穿过）+ spir（呼吸）+ ation」——土面吐汽、叶片呼气，合成蒸散

root: 拉丁 e-（向外）+ vapor「蒸汽」+ trans-（穿过）+ spirare「呼吸」+ -ation；vapor 与 spirare 的更深来源均不确定，整个复合词是近代水文学与农学合成的术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one invisible current: water leaves the ground by two routes, is added into a single flux, is measured as a depth, becomes a farm demand, an accounting term, a heat channel, an ecological loss and finally a metaphor for quiet drainage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一股看不见的水流展开：水经两条路线离地，合成一股通量，被量成水深，成为农田需求、核算项、热量通道、生态损失，最后成为「悄然流失」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two unseen plumes of vapour, one from soil and one from leaves, rise and merge over a field.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股看不见的水汽，一股来自土面，一股来自叶片，在田地上空升起并汇合。

branches.en: TWO CHANNELS: the whole flux and its plant half are the same current seen together or apart.
branches.cn: 两条通道：整体通量与其中的植物部分，是同一股水流的合看与分看。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING: the event becomes a depth of water and a line in the catchment budget.
branches.cn: 核算：事件变成水深数字，变成流域收支表上的一行。

branches.en: FARM DEMAND: what leaves must be replaced, so the flux turns into an irrigation requirement.
branches.cn: 农田需求：失去的必须补回，于是通量变成灌溉要求。

branches.en: TWO LANGUAGES: energy units read the same flux as latent heat, ecology reads it as lost streamflow.
branches.cn: 两套语言：能量单位把同一股通量读作潜热，生态学把它读作失去的径流。

branches.en: METAPHOR: valuable things leave through many small openings, as water leaves a field.
branches.cn: 比喻：有价值之物经许多小口离去，正如水离开田地。

intro.en: Evapotranspiration is a compound of two Latin-derived nouns, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme across four Latin elements and two English suffixes.
intro.cn: evapotranspiration 由两个拉丁来源名词合成，因此可以沿四个拉丁成分与两个英语后缀逐语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor gives vapor, vaporous and vaporize; Latin spirare gives transpire, perspire, inspire and respiration; e- and trans- supply the directions 'out' and 'through'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 衍生 vapor、vaporous 与 vaporize；拉丁 spirare 衍生 transpire、perspire、inspire 与 respiration；e- 与 trans- 提供「向外」与「穿过」两个方向。

items.example: The prefix marks vapour leaving the surface.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出水汽离开地表。

items.example: Vapor rose from the warm asphalt.
items.exampleCN: 水汽从发烫的柏油路面升起。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: Evaporation dried the pan in an hour.
items.exampleCN: 蒸发在一小时内把盘子烤干。

items.example: The prefix marks vapour passing through leaf surfaces.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出水汽穿过叶片表面。

items.example: The root carries the image of breathing out.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「呼出气」的意象。

items.meaning: the act of turning to vapour
items.example: Evaporation from the reservoir peaked in July.
items.exampleCN: 水库蒸发量在七月达到高峰。

items.example: Transpiration cools a leaf in strong sun.
items.exampleCN: 烈日下蒸腾为叶片降温。

items.meaning: to lose water by both channels
items.example: The canopy evapotranspires most of the summer rain.
items.exampleCN: 冠层把夏季雨水的大部分蒸散掉。

items.meaningCN: 以蒸散量为计算依据的
items.exampleCN: 他们采用了以蒸散量为依据的灌溉计划。

definition_zh: 加密；把可读信息转成只有持钥匙者才能还原的编码形式的过程
definition_en: the process of turning readable information into a coded form that only the holder of the key can turn back
core_image: 一封写好的信被锁进铁盒，盒面只剩谁也读不懂的乱码，钥匙挂在大门看守人的腰上
scene: 机房里的灯一直亮着，操作员把钥匙插进读卡器，屏幕上滚过一串谁也读不懂的字符。 Before sending the file, she switched on encryption so that anyone intercepting it would see only random characters.
sceneCN: 这里 encryption 指把可读信息转成密文的过程（第 1 个义项：把明文变成密文的动作）；句意：发送文件之前她开启了加密，中途截获的人只会看到乱码。

pos.zh: 加密；密文化过程；加密方式

derivatives.zh: 加密技术的主张者（罕用）

senses.title: The act of turning plain text into code
senses.titleCN: 把明文变成密文的动作
senses.definition: the act of converting readable information into a coded form by a fixed procedure
senses.definitionCN: 用固定程序把可读信息转换成编码形式的动作
senses.example: Encryption takes place before the message leaves the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 消息离开手机之前就完成了加密。
senses.why: the -tion ending names an action and its result, so the word first denotes the doing of the transformation itself.
senses.whyCN: 词尾表示动作及其结果，因此这个词首先指「做转换」这件事本身。

senses.title: The coded output itself
senses.definition: the unreadable text or data produced by the transformation
senses.definitionCN: 由转换产生、无法直接读懂的文字或数据
senses.example: The intercepted file was pure encryption and told them nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 截获的文件全是密文，他们什么也看不出。
senses.why: the same action noun came to stand for the thing the action leaves behind, the way a building can name the act of building.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作名词也指动作留下的东西，就像「建筑」既可指建造也可指楼房。

senses.title: The field of study and practice
senses.definition: the branch of cryptography that designs and applies such transformations
senses.definitionCN: 密码学中设计并使用这类转换的分支
senses.example: She teaches encryption alongside authentication and key exchange.
senses.exampleCN: 她把加密与身份认证、密钥交换放在一起讲授。
senses.why: a repeated practice becomes a named discipline, and the action noun is reused for the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 反复进行的实践会变成一个有名目的学科，动作名词就被用来指整个领域。

senses.title: Protection of stored data
senses.definition: the encoding of files or disks so that a lost device does not expose its contents
senses.definitionCN: 对文件或磁盘进行编码，使设备丢失时内容不外泄
senses.example: Full-disk encryption saved the company when a laptop was stolen.
senses.exampleCN: 一台笔记本被盗时，全盘加密救了这家公司。
senses.why: data that sits still has no channel to protect, so the word shifted from sending to keeping.
senses.whyCN: 静止的数据没有传输通道可保护，于是这个词从「发送」转向「保存」。

senses.title: Protection of a live connection
senses.definition: the encoding of traffic while it travels between two parties or devices
senses.definitionCN: 数据在两方或两台设备之间传输时进行的编码
senses.example: The chat app applies encryption to every message in transit.
senses.exampleCN: 这款聊天应用对传输中的每条消息都进行加密。
senses.why: the oldest use of secret writing was to guard a message on the road, and networks repeat that situation exactly.
senses.whyCN: 秘密书写最古老的用途就是在路上保护消息，网络只是原样重演了这个场景。

senses.title: Secret writing in history
senses.definition: the old practice of hiding a written message by substitution or transposition
senses.definitionCN: 用替换或换位把书面消息藏起来的古老做法
senses.example: Court letters relied on encryption long before electric machines.
senses.exampleCN: 早在电气机器出现之前，宫廷信件就依赖密文书写。
senses.why: the modern noun inherits a centuries-old craft, so historical ciphers are still called encryption.
senses.whyCN: 现代名词继承了一门数百年的手艺，因此历史密码也仍被称为加密。

senses.title: The mechanism of key and algorithm
senses.definition: the paired rule and secret value that make the transformation reversible
senses.definitionCN: 使这种转换可以逆转的成对规则与秘密数值
senses.example: Weak encryption here means a short key, not a short message.
senses.exampleCN: 这里说的加密强度不足，指的是密钥太短，而不是消息太短。
senses.why: people speak of the machinery by the name of its effect, so a strong key is praised as strong encryption.
senses.whyCN: 人们习惯用效果之名来指机器本身，于是强密钥被称赞为强加密。

senses.title: Deliberate obscurity of meaning
senses.definition: the figurative use for language made needlessly hard to understand
senses.definitionCN: 转指被人为弄得难以理解的语言
senses.example: The report's encryption of plain facts fooled nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告把简单事实写得晦涩，谁也没被唬住。
senses.why: coded writing is unreadable by design, and dull prose that hides its meaning borrows the same image.
senses.whyCN: 密文因设计而不可读，故意掩盖意思的晦涩文章便借用了同一个意象。

intro.en: Encryption joins an English prefix and a Greek root: en-, into, plus kryptos, hidden. The noun ending came through Latin. The machine age gave the old idea of secret writing a technical name.
intro.cn: encryption 由英语前缀与希腊词根拼成：en- 表示「进入」，kryptos 表示「隐藏」，名词词尾经拉丁语而来。机器时代给古老的秘密书写取了一个技术名称。

items.en: Greek kryptos meant hidden or covered, from kryptein, to hide. It described a thing put out of sight, not yet a method of writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 kryptos 意为「隐藏的、被遮盖的」，来自动词 kryptein「隐藏」。它描述的是被藏起来的东西，还不是一种书写方法。

items.en: Latin crypta, borrowed from Greek, named a covered vault or underground chamber. English crypt still means such a chamber.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crypta 借自希腊语，指有顶的地下室或拱形地窖。英语 crypt 至今仍指这种地窖。

items.en: English took crypt for a vault and cryptic for something deliberately obscure, keeping the sense of concealment without any computing meaning.
items.cn: 英语以 crypt 指地窖，以 cryptic 指故意晦涩的事物，保留了「藏」的意思，与计算毫无关系。

items.en: The verb encrypt puts en-, into, before the old root, and the noun adds the Latin ending -tion, so the word literally says putting something into hiding.
items.cn: 动词 encrypt 在旧词根前加 en-「进入」，名词再加拉丁词尾 -tion，字面意思就是「把东西放进隐藏状态」。

items.en: From the twentieth century the word settled on mathematical transformation with a key, first in military signalling and later in computing.
items.cn: 二十世纪起，这个词固定指使用密钥的数学变换，先用于军事通信，后来进入计算机领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of Greek kryptein is not settled, and the older forms sometimes compared with it are reconstructions rather than attested words.
items.cn: 来源不确定：希腊语 kryptein 更早的来源没有定论，常被拿来比较的更古形式属于重构形式，而非有记载的词。

note.en: The first group shares the hidden-root; the second group names neighbouring ways of protecting information.
note.cn: 第一组共享「隐藏」这一词根；第二组是与保护信息相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: The action itself: to turn readable text into code. Encryption is the name of that action or of its result.
entries.definitionCN: 指动作本身：把可读文本变成代码。encryption 则是这个动作或其结果的名称。

entries.definition: The same root with the reversing prefix: the act of turning the code back into readable form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根加表示反向的前缀：把代码还原成可读形式的行为。

entries.definition: Hidden in meaning rather than in code; a cryptic remark puzzles the listener without any cipher.
entries.definitionCN: 指意思难解，而不是被编码；cryptic 的话让人费解，却并没有使用密码。

entries.definition: The old concrete sense of the root: a covered underground room, especially beneath a church.
entries.definitionCN: 词根古老的实体义：有顶的地下室，尤指教堂地下墓室。

entries.definition: Changing data into another representation that anyone with the rule can read; secrecy is not required.
entries.definitionCN: 把数据换成另一种表示，任何人知道规则都能读，并不要求保密。

entries.tag: the old word for the method
entries.definition: A rule for substituting symbols; encryption is the modern technical name for applying such a rule with a key.
entries.definitionCN: 替换符号的规则；encryption 是用密钥执行这类规则的现代技术名称。

entries.definition: Turning data into a fixed-length fingerprint that cannot be turned back; it checks integrity rather than hiding content for later reading.
entries.definitionCN: 把数据变成定长指纹且不可逆，用于校验完整性，而不是隐藏内容供日后阅读。

entries.definition: The broad act of keeping something out of sight; encryption is concealment carried out by a mathematical rule.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西藏起来的泛称；encryption 是用数学规则完成的隐藏。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: kryptos means hidden, so encryption is literally a putting-into-hiding.
normal.cn: kryptos 意为「隐藏」，encryption 字面上就是「放进隐藏状态」。

normal.en: The family lines up neatly: encrypt, encrypted, encryption, decryption.
normal.cn: 同族词排列整齐：encrypt、encrypted、encryption、decryption。

normal.en: Fixed phrases locate the word: encryption key, data encryption, end-to-end encryption.
normal.cn: 固定搭配给它定位：加密密钥、数据加密、端到端加密。

normal.en: The ending marks a process noun, like protection and inspection.
normal.cn: 词尾标记过程名词，与 protection、inspection 同类。

normal.en: Encryption hides the message; decryption brings it back with the key.
normal.cn: 加密把消息藏起来，解密用钥匙把它带回来。

abstract.en: Picture a letter locked in a box whose lid is carved with random grooves, and the grooves are the letter.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信锁进盒子，盒盖刻满看似随机的沟槽，而那些沟槽就是信本身。

abstract.en: Picture a key that is also a sentence, and only the reader who knows the sentence can read the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙同时也是一句话，只有知道这句话的人才能读懂那扇门。

abstract.en: Picture noise on a wire that is perfectly orderly if you stand at the right end of it.
abstract.cn: 想象线路上的噪声乱作一团，可只要站在正确的一端，它其实井然有序。

examples.en: Modern encryption depends on keys that are hard to guess and easy to replace.
examples.cn: 现代加密依赖难以猜测、又便于更换的密钥。

examples.en: The archive keeps its files under encryption so that a lost disk reveals nothing.
examples.cn: 档案馆把文件加密保存，磁盘丢失也不会泄露内容。

examples.en: Without encryption, a public network is simply a room with no walls.
examples.cn: 没有加密，公共网络就是一间没有墙的房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因（en）刻（cry）扑（pt）」——把内容刻进乱码里扑住，就是加密

root: 希腊 kryptos「隐藏的」← kryptein「隐藏」→ 拉丁 crypta「地窖」→ 英语 crypt / cryptic；加前缀 en-「进入」与拉丁词尾 -tion 构成 encryption，二十世纪固定为密钥变换的术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: readable text is put out of sight, then the hidden text, the trade, the stored copy, the travelling message, the old craft, the key mechanism and finally the obscure style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：可读文本先被藏起来，接着是被藏起来的文本、这门行业、静止的副本、传输中的消息、古老手艺、密钥机制，最后是晦涩的文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet locked in a box whose lid carries meaningless grooves, with one key in the world able to open it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满字的纸锁在盒里，盒盖刻着无意义的沟槽，世上只有一把钥匙能打开。

branches.en: ACT AND PRODUCT: the doing of the conversion and the unreadable result it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 动作与成品：转换这件事本身，以及它留下的不可读结果。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND MECHANISM: the field that studies the method, and the rule-and-key pair that carries it out.
branches.cn: 学科与机制：研究这套方法的领域，以及执行它的规则与密钥。

branches.en: TWO SITUATIONS: data standing still on a disk, and data moving along a connection.
branches.cn: 两种场景：静止在磁盘上的数据，以及沿连接传输中的数据。

branches.en: OLD CRAFT: substitution and transposition by hand, the ancestor of the technical procedure.
branches.cn: 古老手艺：手工的替换与换位，是这套技术程序的前身。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE OBSCURITY: language made hard to read without any cipher at all.
branches.cn: 比喻性的晦涩：并没有使用密码，却把语言写得难以读懂。

intro.en: Encryption is assembled from an English prefix, a Greek root and a Latin noun ending; English later added -ed and -ing forms to the verb.
intro.cn: encryption 由英语前缀、希腊词根与拉丁名词词尾拼成；英语后来又给动词加了 -ed、-ing 形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin contribution is the ending -tion, from -tionem, which turns an action verb into a noun of action; crypta is a Greek loan in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的贡献是词尾 -tion（来自 -tionem），把动作动词变成动作名词；crypta 则是拉丁语中的希腊借词。

items.example: The prefix says the message is put into a hidden state.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示消息被放进隐藏状态。

items.example: The adjective describes what cannot be seen.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述看不见的东西。

items.example: The verb is the action behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族背后的动作。

items.example: Latin kept the covered-place sense and passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了「有顶之处」的意思，并传给英语。

items.example: The ending makes the verb into a name for a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成过程的名字。

items.example: The verb is the base from which the noun is formed.
items.exampleCN: 动词是构成该名词的基础。

items.example: An encrypted file has already gone through the steps.
items.exampleCN: 已加密的文件已经走完了这些步骤。

items.example: Encrypting names the work while it is being done.
items.exampleCN: encrypting 指正在进行的工作。

items.example: The same root with de- names the way back.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根加 de- 指回去的路。

definition_zh: 停战；休战协定；（特定语境）停战纪念日
definition_en: an agreement between opposing forces to stop fighting for a period, or the suspension of hostilities itself
core_image: 阵地中央插着一面白旗，两支枪口朝下，怀表停在双方约定的时刻
scene: 战壕两侧的士兵把步枪靠在胸墙上，中间的空地被插上一面白旗，双方军官在泥地里交换签字的纸张。 The two commanders signed an armistice, a formal written halt of the guns, before dawn, and the firing stopped along the line.
sceneCN: 这里 armistice 指「交战双方停止战斗的正式约定」（第 1 个义项：以文书确认的休战安排）；句意为两位指挥官在黎明前签署停战协定，整条战线随即沉寂。可辨识物件：胸墙、步枪、白旗、签字纸张、怀表。

pos.zh: 停战；休战协定；停战期（可数，复数 armistices）

senses.title: A formal agreement to stop fighting
senses.definition: a formal agreement between two opposing forces to suspend fighting, usually while a peace is negotiated
senses.definitionCN: 交战双方暂停战斗的正式约定，通常用于谈判和平期间
senses.example: The two commanders signed an armistice before dawn, and the guns fell silent along the line.
senses.exampleCN: 两位指挥官在黎明前签署停战协定，整条战线随即沉寂。
senses.why: arma 'arms' plus sistere 'to make stand still' gives the literal picture: weapons are made to stand and stop.
senses.whyCN: arma「武器」加 sistere「使立定不动」给出了字面图景：让武器站住、停下。

senses.title: The act of concluding such an agreement
senses.definition: the diplomatic act of negotiating and concluding a suspension of hostilities
senses.definitionCN: 谈判并缔结休战安排的外交行为
senses.example: Delegates argued for weeks before the armistice was signed.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们争论了数周，停战协定才得以签署。
senses.why: the noun can name the event as well as the paper, as with many legal acts in English.
senses.whyCN: 和英语中许多法律行为一样，这个名词既可指文书，也可指事件本身。

senses.title: The period of suspended hostilities
senses.definition: the interval during which the agreement is in force and no fighting takes place
senses.definitionCN: 协定生效、战斗停止的这段时间
senses.example: During the armistice, engineers repaired the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 停战期间，工程人员修复了那座桥。
senses.why: once signed, the agreement fills a stretch of time, and the word shifts from document to duration.
senses.whyCN: 签署之后，协定占据一段时间，词义便从文书转到时段。

senses.title: A local or tactical suspension
senses.definition: a limited halt arranged by local commanders for rescue, burial or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 由当地指挥官为救援、掩埋或谈判安排的有限停火
senses.example: A local armistice let medics recover the wounded.
senses.exampleCN: 一项局部停战让医护得以抬回伤员。
senses.why: the same instrument works at any scale, so a colonel can sign one without ending a war.
senses.whyCN: 同一工具可用于任何规模，因此一名上校也能签署停战而不结束战争。

senses.title: A legally binding instrument
senses.definition: the written terms that fix a line, a timetable and the duties of both sides
senses.definitionCN: 规定分界线、时间表与双方义务的书面条款
senses.example: The armistice set the line of control in legally binding terms.
senses.exampleCN: 停战协定以具有法律约束力的条款确定了控制线。
senses.why: armistice terms often serve as the legal skeleton for a later peace, so the word carries treaty-like weight.
senses.whyCN: 停战条款常成为日后和平的法律骨架，因此这个词带有条约般的分量。

senses.title: The commemorative name Armistice Day
senses.definition: the name given in several countries to the anniversary of the 1918 armistice
senses.definitionCN: 若干国家给一九一八年停战周年所起的名称
senses.example: In several countries Armistice Day marks the eleventh hour of the eleventh day.
senses.exampleCN: 在若干国家，停战纪念日纪念的是十一月十一日的第十一个小时。
senses.why: a single historical armistice became a proper name, so the common noun turned into a calendar label.
senses.whyCN: 一次历史性的停战变成了专名，于是普通名词转为日历标签。

senses.title: A figurative pause in a quarrel
senses.definition: by extension, a temporary halt in any hostile contest, such as a feud or a campaign
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何敌对较量中的暂时中止，如世仇或攻势
senses.example: The rivals reached an armistice in their advertising war.
senses.exampleCN: 对手在广告战中达成了停战。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the military shape: two sides, a line, and a pause that is not yet peace.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留了军事形态：两方、一条线，以及一个还不是和平的暂停。

senses.title: Abstraction: an agreed pause in a hostile relation
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：敌对关系中的约定暂停
senses.definition: any agreed suspension of a hostile relationship, understood as a pause rather than a resolution
senses.definitionCN: 任何敌对关系的约定性中止，理解为暂停而非解决
senses.example: An armistice is not peace; it only stops the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 停战不是和平；它只是让钟停住。
senses.why: the word's deepest sense is procedural: it halts action without settling the dispute, which is why it fits so many conflicts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最深的一层是程序性的：它停止行动，却不解决争端，因此适用于许多冲突。

intro.en: Armistice reached English through French from a medieval Latin compound joining arma 'arms' to sistere 'to stand still'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: armistice 经法语进入英语，来自中世纪拉丁语复合词，把 arma「武器」与 sistere「站住」连接起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arma, a plural noun, meant 'arms, weapons, equipment'; the related verb armare meant 'to equip for war'.
items.cn: arma 是复数名词，意为「武器、装备」；相关动词 armare 意为「为战争装备」。

items.en: Sistere meant 'to cause to stand, to stop, to halt'; it is related to stare 'to stand', and the suffix -stitium named a stopping.
items.cn: sistere 意为「使站立、使停止、使停下」；它与 stare「站立」相关，后缀 -stitium 表示「停止」。

items.en: Medieval Latin armistitium combined the two ideas as 'a standing still of arms', the literal ancestor of the modern word.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 armistitium 把两个概念合成「武器的静止」，是现代词的字面前身。

items.en: The French form armistice spread in the seventeenth century and entered English soon after; early uses concerned temporary suspensions in European wars.
items.cn: 法语形式 armistice 在十七世纪流行，随后进入英语；早期用法指欧洲战争中的暂时休战。

items.en: After the armistice of 11 November 1918, the date was observed as Armistice Day in several countries; some later renamed it for all war dead.
items.cn: 一九一八年十一月十一日停战之后，若干国家把这一天作为停战日纪念；有些国家后来改名以纪念所有战争死者。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English citation and suffix analysis): dictionaries do not fix the earliest English use, and the division of -stitium between sistere and statio is an interpretation rather than a recorded fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与后缀分析）：辞书未确定最早的英语用例；把 -stitium 归于 sistere 还是 statio 只是一种解释，并非有记录的事实。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the arms or standing-still stock, easily confused with armistice; group two holds the neighbouring stop-fighting terms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「武器」或「立定」词干、易与 armistice 混淆的词；第二组是邻近的「停止战斗」类词。

entries.definition: Military equipment and the process of building it up; it shares arma with armistice but means arming, not disarming.
entries.definitionCN: 指军事装备及扩充军备的过程；与 armistice 同出 arma，但意思是「武装」而非「停止武装」。

entries.definition: Protective covering for the body or a vehicle; it comes through Old French from Latin armatura, a derivative of armare.
entries.definitionCN: 指护身或护车的装甲；经古法语来自拉丁 armatura，是 armare 的派生词。

entries.definition: A stop in fighting agreed for a short time; it is the everyday older synonym and often implies a shorter pause than armistice.
entries.definitionCN: 指短时间约定的停火；这是更早的日常同义词，通常暗示比 armistice 更短的暂停。

entries.definition: The boundary fixed by an armistice; the phrase names a place, while armistice names the agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 指停战协定确定的界线；该短语指地点，而 armistice 指协定。

entries.definition: An order or agreement to stop firing; it can be local or informal, whereas armistice usually implies a formal instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 指停止射击的命令或约定，可局部、可非正式；armistice 通常暗示正式文书。

entries.definition: A binding agreement between states; a peace treaty settles the war, while an armistice only suspends it.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家间有约束力的协定；和平条约解决战争，而停战只把战争暂停。

entries.definition: The formal surrender of a force on stated terms; it is one-sided, unlike an armistice between equals.
entries.definitionCN: 指一支部队按条件正式投降；它是单方面的，不同于对等双方的停战。

entries.definition: A return from combat readiness to normal duty; it is an internal order, not a bargain between enemies.
entries.definitionCN: 指从战备状态回到正常值勤；这是内部命令，不是敌我之间的交易。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the historical date and the real compounds built on the same stem.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、那个历史日期，以及同词干构成的真实复合词。

normal.en: arma 'arms' + sistere 'stand still': arms made to stand still.
normal.cn: arma「武器」+ sistere「站住」：让武器站住不动。

normal.en: The medieval form armistitium is the same picture written out: a stopping of arms.
normal.cn: 中世纪形式 armistitium 把这个图景写全：武器的停止。

normal.en: The eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month is the 1918 armistice.
normal.cn: 十一月十一日第十一个小时，就是一九一八年的停战时刻。

normal.en: The family runs arms, armament, disarm, disarmament, armoury.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arms、armament、disarm、disarmament、armoury。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with armour: one stops the guns, the other stops the bullet.
normal.cn: 不要与 armour 混淆：一个让枪停下，一个让子弹停下。

abstract.en: Picture two boxers touching gloves: the fight pauses, but the match is not decided.
abstract.cn: 想象两名拳手碰拳：打斗暂停了，但比赛尚未分出胜负。

abstract.en: Picture a clock stopped by agreement rather than by damage.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟是被约定停住的，而不是被损坏停住的。

abstract.en: Picture a door held ajar between two rooms: neither closed nor open.
abstract.cn: 想象两个房间之间一扇半开的门：既没关上，也没敞开。

examples.en: The armistice left the city divided along a temporary line.
examples.cn: 停战协定沿一条临时界线把城市分开。

examples.en: Neither side trusted the armistice to last through the winter.
examples.cn: 双方都不相信停战能维持整个冬天。

examples.en: A signed armistice bought time for the peace conference.
examples.cn: 签署停战协定为和平会议争取了时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「arm（武器）+ st（停住）+ ice（冰）」——武器冻住不动 → 停战

root: 拉丁 arma「武器」+ sistere「使站住」，中世纪拉丁 armistitium 字面为「武器的静止」。sistere 与 stare「站立」相关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one act: weapons are made to stand still. The act becomes a signed document, then a stretch of time, then a local arrangement, then a legal instrument, then a calendar name, then a metaphor for any quarrel and finally a general name for a pause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个动作展开：让武器立定。这个动作先成为签署的文书，再成为一段时间，再成为局部安排，再成为法律工具，再成为日历名称，再成为任何争执的比喻，最后成为「暂停」的通称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rifles stacked upright with a white flag between them, a watch stopped at the agreed hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：步枪竖着架起，中间一面白旗，怀表停在约定的时刻。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: words on paper make the weapons stand still and bind both sides.
branches.cn: 文书：纸上的文字让武器立定，并约束双方。

branches.en: THE EVENT AND ITS DURATION: signing opens a stretch of quiet.
branches.cn: 事件与时长：签署打开一段安静。

branches.en: THE DATE: one armistice becomes a name on the calendar.
branches.cn: 日期：一次停战变成日历上的名称。

branches.en: THE SMALL SCALE: the same act shrinks to a colonel's local bargain.
branches.cn: 小尺度：同一动作可缩小为上校的局部交易。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any feud can borrow the white flag, because a pause is not a settlement.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何争执都能借这面白旗，因为暂停并不等于解决。

intro.en: Armistice is a Latin compound whose two halves still build other English words, so it can be read as prefix-like element plus root.
intro.cn: armistice 是拉丁复合词，两个部分仍构成其他英语词，因此可按「前成分加词根」读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin arma gives arm, armament, disarm and armoury; Latin sistere gives insist, resist, persist and assist, all through the sense of standing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 arma 衍生 arm、armament、disarm 与 armoury；拉丁 sistere 经「站立」之义衍生 insist、resist、persist 与 assist。

items.example: The legion laid down its arma.

items.structure: sistere (Latin verb, to cause to stand)
items.example: The guard was ordered to sistere.
The armistice held for six weeks.

items.meaning: equipment for war; the act of arming
items.example: Naval armament expanded before the war.
The patrol was disarmed at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 巡逻队在门口被解除武装。

items.meaning: a place where weapons are stored
items.example: The armoury kept the reserve rifles.
She insisted on a written term.
items.exampleCN: 她坚持要有一项书面条款。

items.example: The unit resisted for a week.
Both generals initialled the armistice agreement.
items.exampleCN: 两位将军草签了停战协议。

definition_zh: n. 合并，整合；巩固，加强
definition_en: the joining of parts into one, or the making of something stronger
core_image: 散沙被压实成一块坚固的砖
scene: 两家公司的合并节省了大量成本。 The consolidation of the two firms saved a great deal in costs.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：consolidation 指合并；句意是两家公司的合并节省了大量成本。

senses.title: Joining into one
senses.definition: the joining of separate parts into one body
senses.definitionCN: 把分散部分合成一体
senses.example: The consolidation of two firms saved money.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司合并省下开支。
senses.why: Latin solidus means solid.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 solidus 意为坚实。

senses.title: Making firm
senses.definition: the act of making something stronger and more stable
senses.definitionCN: 使事物更强更稳
senses.example: The army needed consolidation of its gains.
senses.exampleCN: 军队需要巩固战果。
senses.why: What is joined is also made solid.
senses.whyCN: 合在一起的东西也被压实。

intro.en: Consolidation is Latin consolidare, to make solid, as a noun.
intro.cn: consolidation 是拉丁语 consolidare（使坚实）的名词形。

items.en: Solidus means solid.
items.cn: solidus 意为坚实的。

items.en: Consolidare means to make solid.
items.cn: consolidare 意为使坚实。

items.en: Consolidatio names the making firm.
items.cn: consolidatio 指巩固。

items.en: English used it of joined forces.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用它指合兵一处。

items.en: Business used it of merged firms.
items.cn: 二十世纪商业用它指公司合并。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the consolid- stem; the near-meaning group names merging and firming.
note.cn: 形近组共享 consolid- 词干；近义组列出合并与加强。

entries.definition: To join or make firm.
entries.definitionCN: 合并或巩固。

entries.definition: Joined into one.
entries.definitionCN: 合并成一体 的。

entries.definition: Firm and not hollow.
entries.definitionCN: 坚实不空的。

entries.definition: The combining of two companies.
entries.definitionCN: 两家公司合为一体。

entries.definition: The act of making into one.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为一体。

entries.definition: The act of making stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 使更强。

entries.definition: The joining of parts into a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把部分合成整体。

normalIntro.en: Consolidation packs many parts into one firm mass.
normalIntro.cn: consolidation 把许多部分压成一团坚实之物。

normal.en: Solidus means solid.

normal.en: Consolidare means to make solid.

normal.en: Firms consolidate into one group.

normal.en: Armies consolidate their gains.
normal.cn: 军队巩固战果。

normal.en: The noun is consolidation.
normal.cn: 名词是 consolidation。

abstract.cn: 松沙压成砖。

abstract.en: Several voices settling on one note.
abstract.cn: 几个声音落向同一个音。

abstract.en: Scattered troops closing ranks.
abstract.cn: 散兵收拢队形。

examples.en: The consolidation of the industry cut jobs.
examples.cn: 行业整合削减了岗位。

examples.en: A year of consolidation followed the merger.
examples.cn: 合并后经历了一年的整合。

examples.en: Debt consolidation can lower monthly payments.
examples.cn: 债务整合可降低月供。

sensesIntro.en: Bringing parts together, and pressing them firm.
sensesIntro.cn: 把部分聚到一起，并压实使其坚固。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose sand pressed into one hard brick
core.cn: 核心意象：松沙压成一块硬砖

branches.en: Two firms signing one name.
branches.cn: 两家公司签下一个名字。

branches.en: Debts gathered into one loan.
branches.cn: 合成一笔的债务。

branches.en: A hill fortified after a win.
branches.cn: 得胜后加固的山头。

branches.en: A habit made firm by practice.
branches.cn: 练习使之牢固的习惯。

branches.en: Joined so that it holds.
branches.cn: 合而使其稳固。

intro.en: Consolidation grows from solids made one.
intro.cn: consolidation 由「变坚实、合为一体」而来。

latinIntro.en: Latin solidus is solid and consolidare is to make solid.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solidus 意为坚实，consolidare 意为使坚实。

definition_zh: 虚拟现实；由计算机生成、可沉浸其中的三维环境；沉浸式头显技术及相关产业
definition_en: a computer-generated environment that a person can enter and interact with, usually through a headset
core_image: 参观者戴上头显，眼前出现一座可以走动查看的古罗马市场
scene: 参观者戴上头显，眼前出现一座可以走动查看的古罗马市场。 Virtual reality let her walk through the market without leaving the room.
sceneCN: 这里指由计算机生成、可沉浸其中的三维环境（第 1 个义项：沉浸式虚拟环境）；句意为虚拟现实让她足不出户就走遍了那座市场。图中可辨识物件：头显、手柄、市场柱廊、地毯边界。

pos.zh: 虚拟现实；沉浸式计算机生成环境

senses.title: An immersive generated environment
senses.definition: a three-dimensional world produced by a computer that a person can enter and move around in
senses.definitionCN: 由计算机生成、人可以进入并在其中移动的三维世界
senses.example: The museum built a virtual reality of the drowned town.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆造了一个被淹小镇的虚拟现实。
senses.why: Virtual supplies the software-made existence and reality supplies the claim that it is a world, not a picture.
senses.whyCN: 前一词提供软件造出的存在，后一词提供「这是一个世界而非一幅画」的主张。

senses.title: The technology and industry
senses.definition: the hardware, software and business built around immersive computer environments
senses.definitionCN: 围绕沉浸式计算机环境形成的硬件、软件与产业
senses.example: Virtual reality is now a small but growing industry.
senses.exampleCN: 虚拟现实如今是一个规模不大却在增长的产业。
senses.why: When a phrase names a medium, it also names the companies that make and sell it.
senses.whyCN: 当一个说法命名一种媒介，它也命名了制造与销售它的公司。

senses.title: The headset experience
senses.definition: the experience of wearing a display close to the eyes that fills the field of view
senses.definitionCN: 戴上贴近双眼、占满视野的显示器所获得的体验
senses.example: The film is shown in virtual reality, with the audience seated in moving chairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片以虚拟现实方式放映，观众坐在会动的椅子上。
senses.why: The headset is the door through which the generated world becomes a bodily experience.
senses.whyCN: 头显是那扇门，生成的世界由它变成身体经验。

senses.title: Training and simulation
senses.definition: the use of generated environments to practise tasks that would be costly or dangerous in life
senses.definitionCN: 用生成环境练习在现实中昂贵或危险的任务
senses.example: Pilots use virtual reality to rehearse emergency landings.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员用虚拟现实演练紧急着陆。
senses.why: If the world is convincing enough, practice inside it transfers to the body outside it.
senses.whyCN: 只要那个世界足够可信，其中的练习就能转移到外面的身体上。

senses.title: Shared social space
senses.definition: a networked generated world in which several people appear to one another as avatars
senses.definitionCN: 若干人以化身相互出现的联网生成世界
senses.example: They held a family reunion in virtual reality.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一场虚拟现实里办了家庭聚会。
senses.why: A world that several people can enter at once becomes a place where relationships happen.
senses.whyCN: 一个多人可同时进入的世界，就成了关系发生的场所。

senses.title: An art form
senses.definition: a medium in which artists build spaces and experiences rather than flat images
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家在其中搭建空间与体验、而非平面图像的媒介
senses.example: The installation treats virtual reality as sculpture you can walk inside.
senses.exampleCN: 这件装置把虚拟现实当作可以走进去的雕塑。
senses.why: Art has always made stand-in worlds; this one surrounds the viewer instead of facing them.
senses.whyCN: 艺术一向在造替身世界；这一个把观者围住，而不是面对观者。

senses.title: Therapeutic exposure
senses.definition: the controlled presentation of a feared situation in a generated environment as part of therapy
senses.definitionCN: 在生成环境中受控呈现所恐惧的情境，作为治疗的一部分
senses.example: Virtual reality helped him approach the lift without panic.
senses.exampleCN: 虚拟现实帮他不再惊恐地接近电梯。
senses.why: A feared place can be visited safely when it is only effective, not physical.
senses.whyCN: 当可怕的地点只是有效而非实体，人就能安全地造访它。

senses.title: A fictional setting
senses.definition: a generated world presented in a story as a place where characters live or are trapped
senses.definitionCN: 故事中作为人物生活或被困之地的生成世界
senses.example: The novel describes a virtual reality that no one can leave.
senses.exampleCN: 那部小说描写了一个无人能离开的虚拟现实。
senses.why: Fiction uses the technology as a setting, and the phrase becomes a name for a world with rules.
senses.whyCN: 虚构作品把这技术当作设定，这个说法于是成为一种有规则世界的名字。

senses.title: A constructed false reality
senses.titleCN: 被人为构造的虚假现实
senses.definition: a version of reality so shaped by others that it replaces what is actually there
senses.definitionCN: 被他人塑造到取代实际情形的一种现实版本
senses.example: The advertisement sells a virtual reality of perfect families.
senses.exampleCN: 那则广告贩卖一种完美家庭的虚假现实。
senses.why: The oldest sense of virtual is 'effective though not formal', and here the effect has swallowed the fact.
senses.whyCN: 前一词最古老的意思是「有效但非正式」，在这里效果吞掉了事实。

intro.en: Virtual reality joins virtual, from Late Latin virtualis 'having power', and reality, from Latin realis 'of a thing', from res. The phrase was used in French in the 1930s and was popularised in English by Jaron Lanier in 1987; the exact first use of the English phrase is source uncertain.
intro.cn: virtual reality 由 virtual（晚期拉丁 virtualis「有力量的」）与 reality（拉丁 realis「事物的」，源自 res）组合。该短语在二十世纪三十年代已见于法语，英语则由贾龙·拉尼尔于一九八七年推广；英语短语最早出现的准确出处来源不确定。

items.en: Late Latin virtualis meant having power or producing an effect, and English virtual kept the sense of what is effective without being a separate object.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 virtualis 指有力量或能产生效果，英语 virtual 保留了「有效而非独立实物」之义。

items.en: Latin realis meant belonging to a thing, from res 'thing'; English reality names what actually exists rather than what merely appears.
items.cn: 拉丁 realis 指属于某物的，源自 res「事物」；英语 reality 命名实际存在者，而非仅仅显现者。

items.en: French writers used la realite virtuelle in the 1930s for an artificial or imagined reality, a use that predates the headset.
items.cn: 法语作者在二十世纪三十年代已用 la realite virtuelle 指人造或想象的真实，早于头显出现。

items.en: Jaron Lanier is generally credited with popularising the English phrase in 1987, though earlier uses exist and the first written instance is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为贾龙·拉尼尔在一九八七年使英语短语流行，但更早的用法存在，最早书面实例来源不确定。

items.en: Research labs in the late 1980s and 1990s built gloves and head-mounted displays, turning the phrase from an idea into equipment.
items.cn: 二十世纪八十年代末至九十年代，研究实验室造出手套与头戴显示器，把这个短语从想法变成设备。

items.en: Consumer headsets in the 2010s made the phrase common in shops and schools, and it now also names a whole industry.
items.cn: 二十一世纪一十年代的消费级头显使这个短语常见于商店与学校，如今它也指整个产业。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like virtual reality; the second group names neighbouring ideas in the same field.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「virtual reality」相近；第二组是同一领域里意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: The first element, meaning effective or software-made rather than physically separate.
entries.definitionCN: 第一部分，意为有效的或软件造出的，而非独立实体。

entries.definition: The second element, naming what actually exists.
entries.definitionCN: 第二部分，命名实际存在之物。

entries.definition: The abstract quality of being virtual, not a name for the immersive world.
entries.definitionCN: 「虚拟性」这一抽象性质，不是沉浸世界的名称。

entries.definition: The adjective behind reality; it contrasts with what is simulated.
entries.definitionCN: reality 背后的形容词，与模拟之物相对。

entries.definition: An artistic aim to show things as they are, which is not the same as making a world.
entries.definitionCN: 力求按本来面目呈现的艺术主张，与造一个世界不同。

entries.definition: Digital content laid over the live view rather than replacing it.
entries.definitionCN: 把数字内容叠加在实时画面上，而不是取代它。

entries.definition: A blend in which real and generated objects share one space and interact.
entries.definitionCN: 真实与生成之物共处一个空间并相互作用的混合。

entries.definition: An imitation of a system, often on a flat screen and not entered bodily.
entries.definitionCN: 对系统的模仿，常在平面屏幕上，不以身体进入。

entries.definition: A persistent shared online world, broader than one headset experience.
entries.definitionCN: 持续存在的共享网络世界，比单次头显体验更广。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin roots, the real dated history and real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实拉丁词根、真实可考年代与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Virtual comes from Latin virtus 'power', so the phrase claims a world that is effective without being physical.
normal.cn: virtual 来自拉丁 virtus「力量」，因此这个短语主张一个有效却非实体的世界。

normal.en: Reality comes from Latin res 'thing', so the second word insists that this is a world, not a picture.
normal.cn: reality 来自拉丁 res「事物」，因此第二个词坚持这是一个世界，不是一幅画。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: headset, training, game, experience, exposure therapy.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：头显、训练、游戏、体验、暴露疗法。

normal.en: The abbreviation VR is used in shops and research papers alike.
normal.cn: 缩写 VR 在商店与研究论文里同样通用。

normal.en: The phrase was popularised in 1987 and reached consumers in the 2010s.
normal.cn: 这个短语在一九八七年流行，并在二十一世纪一十年代进入消费者市场。

abstract.en: A headset is a doorway; the world behind it has no floor you can fall through.
abstract.cn: 头显是一道门，门后的世界没有能摔下去的地板。

abstract.en: The body stays in the room while the eyes travel.
abstract.cn: 身体留在房间里，眼睛却出门远行。

abstract.en: When the effect is strong enough, the absence of the place stops mattering.
abstract.cn: 当效果足够强，地点的不存在就不再要紧。

examples.en: Virtual reality made it possible to rehearse the surgery before the patient arrived.
examples.cn: 虚拟现实让医生能在病人到来之前演练这台手术。

examples.en: The school uses virtual reality to show students places they cannot visit.
examples.cn: 学校用虚拟现实给学生展示他们去不了的地方。

examples.en: He spent the afternoon in virtual reality, building a house no one could live in.
examples.cn: 他一下午都泡在虚拟现实里，造一栋没人能住的房子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「虚拟 + 现实」——眼睛进了另一个世界，身体还坐在原地

root: virtual 源自晚期拉丁 virtualis「有力量的」；reality 源自拉丁 realis「事物的」，更早为 res「事物」。该短语二十世纪三十年代见于法语，英语由拉尼尔于一九八七年推广；最早英语书面用例来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one entered world: a generated environment, an industry, a headset experience, a training ground, a shared social space, an art form, a therapy, a fictional setting, and finally a false reality that replaces the real one.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个可进入的世界：生成的环境、一个产业、头显体验、训练场、共享社交空间、艺术形式、治疗场景、虚构设定，最后是取代真实世界的虚假现实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a headset opens onto a market one can walk through while the body stays in the room.
core.cn: 核心意象：头显打开一座可以走动的市场，身体却留在房间里。

branches.en: THE WORLD AND THE DOOR: a generated place exists, and a display close to the eyes lets the body enter it.
branches.cn: 世界与门：一个生成的地点存在，贴近双眼的显示器让身体进入。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRY: the phrase names the hardware, software and companies around the world.
branches.cn: 产业：这个说法命名围绕该世界的硬件、软件与公司。

branches.en: THE REHEARSAL AND THE CURE: dangerous tasks and feared places are met safely inside the generated world.
branches.cn: 演练与疗愈：危险任务与恐惧场所在生成世界里被安全地面对。

branches.en: THE SHARED AND THE MADE: several people meet as avatars, and artists build spaces to walk inside.
branches.cn: 共享与创作：若干人以化身相见，艺术家搭建可走入的空间。

branches.en: THE STORY AND THE SUBSTITUTE: fiction uses the world as a setting, and advertisement uses it to replace the real one.
branches.cn: 故事与替代品：虚构把它当设定，广告用它取代真实。

intro.en: Virtual reality is a two-word term built from Late Latin virtualis and Latin realis.
intro.cn: virtual reality 是由晚期拉丁 virtualis 与拉丁 realis 构成的双词术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin virtus gives virtualis; Latin res gives realis; English joins the two adjectives and later makes them a fixed phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 virtus 衍生 virtualis，拉丁 res 衍生 realis；英语把两个形容词连起来，后来固定成短语。

items.example: The first element of the phrase.
The second element insists on a world.
items.exampleCN: 第二部分坚持这是一个世界。
英语缩短了那个拉丁形容词。

items.example: English built the noun on realis.
items.exampleCN: 英语在 realis 上造出名词。

items.example: The abbreviation carries the phrase into daily use.
items.exampleCN: 缩写把短语带入日常使用。

items.meaning: a person who works in virtual reality

items.exampleCN: 它构成 reality 与 virtuality。

definition_zh: 航空航天（地球大气层与外层空间的合称）；航空航天工业
definition_en: the earth’s atmosphere together with outer space, considered as one region; the industry that builds aircraft and spacecraft
core_image: 把大气层和外层空间当成同一片地方
scene: 厂房一头装着机翼，另一头装着火箭整流罩。 The aerospace plant employs half the town.
sceneCN: 这里 aerospace 是「航空航天工业」（第 2 个义项：制造飞行器与航天器的产业）；句意为这家航空航天工厂雇了镇上一半的人。核心画面是把大气层与外层空间当成同一片地方。

pos.zh: 航空航天；航空航天工业

derivatives.zh: 同族复合词，由 air 加 space 构成，义为「空域」，只指大气层内
同族复合词，由 space 加 craft 构成，义为「航天器」
同族复合词，由 aero- 加 drome「跑道」构成，义为「机场」

senses.title: The atmosphere and outer space as one region
senses.definition: the earth’s atmosphere and the space beyond it, treated together as a single continuous region
senses.definitionCN: 地球大气层与其外的空间，被当作一个连续的整体区域
senses.example: Vehicles crossing aerospace must survive both air and vacuum.
senses.exampleCN: 穿越航空航天的飞行器必须同时承受空气与真空。
senses.why: Aero means air and space means the void beyond it, so the compound deliberately refuses to draw a line where the atmosphere thins away.
senses.whyCN: aero 意为「空气」，space 意为其外的虚空，所以这个复合词刻意不在大气变稀处划线。

senses.title: The industry that builds for both
senses.definition: the sector of industry that designs and manufactures aircraft, missiles and spacecraft
senses.definitionCN: 设计制造飞行器、导弹与航天器的工业部门
senses.example: Aerospace is the region’s largest employer.
senses.exampleCN: 航空航天业是该地区最大的雇主。
senses.why: Once the region had one name, the factories serving it took that name too, which is how a word for a place became a word for an industry.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这片区域有了统一的名字，为它服务的工厂也就沿用了这个名字——一个地点词由此变成产业词。

intro.en: Aerospace is a modern American compound, coined because rockets made the old border between air and space useless.
intro.cn: aerospace 是现代美式复合词，它的出现是因为火箭让空气与空间之间的旧边界失效了。

items.en: Greek aer, air, supplies the first element through the combining form aero-.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer「空气」通过组合形式 aero- 提供第一个成分。

items.en: Latin spatium meant space, extent or room, and it gave English space and spacious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 spatium 意为「空间、范围、余地」，它给出英语 space 与 spacious。

items.en: The combining form aero- became productive in the nineteenth century with balloons and early flying machines.
items.cn: 组合形式 aero- 在十九世纪随气球与早期飞行器变得能产。

items.en: Aerospace was coined in the United States in the nineteen fifties, when a single vehicle might cross both air and vacuum.
items.cn: aerospace 于二十世纪五十年代在美国造出，当时同一飞行器可能同时穿越空气与真空。

items.en: The word quickly shifted from a region to the industry serving it, and it is now usually met as an attributive noun.
items.cn: 该词很快从区域义转为服务该区域的产业义，如今多以名词作定语的形式出现。

note.en: The look-alike group separates aerospace from airspace, which stops at the atmosphere; the near-meaning group lists the two fields it joins.
note.cn: 形近组把 aerospace 与只到大气层为止的 airspace 区分开；近义组列出它所连接的两个领域。

entries.definition: The portion of the atmosphere controlled or used by aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 由航空器管制或使用的那部分大气层。

entries.definition: An airfield, from aero- plus drome, a running place.
entries.definitionCN: 机场，由 aero- 加 drome「跑动之处」构成。

entries.definition: An astronaut, a person who travels in space.
entries.definitionCN: 宇航员，在太空中旅行的人。

entries.definition: Flight within the atmosphere only.
entries.definitionCN: 仅在大气层内的飞行。

entries.definition: Flight beyond the atmosphere only.
entries.definitionCN: 仅在大气层外的飞行。

entries.definition: The region beyond the earth’s atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 地球大气层之外的区域。

normalIntro.en: Aerospace is aero plus space: air and the void beyond, written as one word.
normalIntro.cn: aerospace 就是 aero 加 space：空气与其外的虚空，写成一个词。

normal.en: Aero covers the atmosphere; space covers what lies beyond it.
normal.cn: aero 覆盖大气层；space 覆盖其外的一切。

normal.en: Airspace stops where the air stops; aerospace does not.
normal.cn: airspace 在空气尽头停下；aerospace 不停。

normal.en: The word is usually a modifier: aerospace industry, aerospace engineering.
normal.cn: 这个词通常作定语：aerospace industry、aerospace engineering。

normal.en: It was coined in the nineteen fifties, so it is younger than aviation.
normal.cn: 它造于二十世纪五十年代，所以比 aviation 年轻。

normal.en: One word, two domains, one factory floor.
normal.cn: 一个词，两个领域，一个厂房。

abstract.en: Picture a single road that runs from a runway to an orbit without a border post.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从跑道通到轨道、中途没有边检站的公路。

abstract.en: Imagine a map where the sky and the vacuum are coloured the same.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天空与真空被涂成同一种颜色的地图。

abstract.en: Think of a factory whose left door opens onto clouds and whose right door opens onto stars.
abstract.cn: 想象一家工厂，左门通向云层，右门通向星辰。

examples.en: The aerospace sector has doubled its output in five years.
examples.cn: 航空航天部门在五年内产量翻了一番。

examples.en: She studies aerospace engineering with a focus on propulsion.
examples.cn: 她攻读航空航天工程，主攻推进系统。

examples.en: Aerospace begins where the air is thick and ends where it is gone.
examples.cn: 航空航天始于空气稠密处，止于空气消失处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱儿罗斯佩斯」——爱儿（aero）罗（o）斯佩斯（space），空气与太空连成一片，就是航空航天。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」的组合形式 aero-，加拉丁语 spatium「空间」经古法语 espace 进入英语的 space，于二十世纪五十年代在美国复合成 aerospace，指大气层与外层空间的整体。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are one idea at two scales: a continuous region from thick air to vacuum, and then the industry that builds machines for the whole of it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一想法的两种尺度：从稠密空气到真空的连续区域，以及为这整片区域制造机器的工业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air and the void beyond treated as one place
core.cn: 核心意象：把空气与其外的虚空当成同一个地方

branches.en: The region named as a continuous whole.
branches.cn: 作为连续整体命名的区域。

branches.en: The factories named after that region.
branches.cn: 以该区域命名的工厂。

branches.en: Both refuse to stop at the atmosphere.
branches.cn: 两者都不在大气层处止步。

branches.en: A vehicle must survive air and vacuum.
branches.cn: 飞行器须同时承受空气与真空。

branches.en: The word now works mainly as a modifier.
branches.cn: 该词如今主要作定语使用。

intro.en: Aerospace is a compound of two combining forms rather than a root plus suffix, so its relatives are other compounds of air and space.
intro.cn: aerospace 是两个组合形式的复合，而非词根加后缀，因此其亲属词是其他「空气」与「空间」的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Aero- is Greek in origin while space comes from Latin spatium, so this compound mixes the two classical layers.
latinIntro.cn: aero- 源自希腊语，而 space 来自拉丁语 spatium，因此这个复合词混合了两个古典层。

latinEntries.example: Spatium is the source of space.
latinEntries.exampleCN: spatium 是 space 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Aer supplies the aero- of aerospace.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 提供 aerospace 中的 aero-。

definition_zh: 紧缩；节俭，清苦；朴素，无装饰；严峻；艰苦时期；苦行
definition_en: the quality of being plain and without comfort or ornament; strict economy in spending, especially by a government; a practice of self-denial
core_image: 把装饰与多余的东西一件件拿走，只剩必需
scene: 危机之后，政府砍掉补贴，公共开支一路收紧。 The government defended austerity as a way to cut the deficit.
sceneCN: 这里 austerity 是「财政紧缩」（第 1 个义项）；句意是政府为削减赤字而为紧缩政策辩护。

pos.zh: 名词：紧缩；节俭；朴素；严峻；苦行

derivatives.zh: 同族形容词：朴素的；严峻的
加副词后缀：朴素地；严峻地
加性质后缀：朴素；严峻（罕用）

senses.title: Strict cuts in public spending
senses.definition: a government policy of reducing spending and borrowing, usually after a crisis
senses.definitionCN: 政府削减开支与借贷的政策，通常在危机之后推行
senses.example: Austerity reduced the deficit but closed two libraries.
senses.exampleCN: 紧缩降低了赤字，却关掉两座图书馆。
senses.why: The old sense of harsh self-denial was applied to a state: the country must live on less, as a monk does.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「克己受苦」义被用到国家身上：国家也得像修士那样少花少用。

senses.title: Plain living without comfort
senses.definition: a way of living that allows no luxury and few comforts
senses.definitionCN: 不容奢侈、少有舒适的生活方式
senses.example: They chose austerity for the sake of the work.
senses.exampleCN: 为了工作，他们选择了清苦的生活。
senses.why: Dryness becomes a moral choice: what is stripped away is pleasure, not necessity.
senses.whyCN: 「干涩」变成一种道德选择：被抽掉的是享受，而不是必需。

senses.title: Absence of ornament
senses.definition: the quality of a design or style that uses no decoration
senses.definitionCN: 设计或风格不加装饰的性质
senses.example: The austerity of the chapel suits the landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 小教堂的素净与这片风景相称。
senses.why: What is dry and bare in taste becomes bare in appearance, and bareness can be praised as honesty.
senses.whyCN: 味道上的干涩转到外观上的光秃，而这种光秃可以被赞为诚实。

senses.title: Severity of manner
senses.definition: a strict, unsmiling manner that shows no softness
senses.definitionCN: 严格、不带笑意、毫无柔和的态度
senses.example: The austerity of his face frightened new students.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上的严峻让新生害怕。
senses.why: A person who denies himself comfort often denies others warmth, so the word moves from things to faces.
senses.whyCN: 对自己不给舒适的人，往往对别人也不给温和，于是这个词从物品转到面孔。

senses.title: Hard conditions of a period
senses.definition: the harsh conditions of a time when goods and money are short, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 物资与钱款短缺时期的艰苦状况，常用复数
senses.example: The austerities of the war years shaped her habits.
senses.exampleCN: 战争年代的匮乏塑造了她的习惯。
senses.why: When hardship is imposed rather than chosen, the plural names the separate privations people endured.
senses.whyCN: 当艰苦是被强加而非自选时，复数形式指人们挨过的一桩桩匮乏。

senses.title: Religious self-denial
senses.definition: a practice of fasting or bodily discipline undertaken for spiritual reasons, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 出于精神目的而进行的斋戒或身体磨炼，通常用复数
senses.example: Lenten austerities included fasting and silence.
senses.exampleCN: 四旬期的苦行包括斋戒与静默。
senses.why: This is the oldest English use: the dry, harsh life chosen to train the soul.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最老的用法：为磨炼灵魂而自选的干涩严苦生活。

intro.en: Austerity comes from a Greek word for dry and harsh, through Latin; what dries the mouth became what strips away comfort.
intro.cn: austerity 出自希腊语表示「干燥、粗硬」的词，经拉丁语而来；让嘴发干的东西，变成了抽走舒适的东西。

items.en: Greek austeros meant dry and harsh, used of wind, taste and character; the root behind it is connected with dryness.
items.cn: 希腊语 austeros 意为「干燥、粗硬」，风、味道与性格都能用；其背后的词根与「干燥」有关。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as austerus, harsh, dry or sour, describing what puckers the mouth.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 austerus，意为「粗硬、干燥、酸涩」，描述让嘴收缩的东西。

items.en: The noun austeritas named the quality of harshness or strictness.
items.cn: 名词 austeritas 指粗硬或严格这种性质。

items.en: Old French austérité carried the noun into the western languages in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 austérité 在十四世纪把这个名词带入西欧语言。

items.en: English took the word for severity of life and manner, especially the self-denial of religious discipline.
items.cn: 英语借入后指生活与态度的严苦，尤其是宗教修行中的克己。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became a political term for cuts in public spending, while design still uses it for plainness.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词成为削减公共开支的政治术语，而设计领域仍用它指朴素。

note.en: The look-alike group mixes the true family with two words that only share the ending; the near-meaning group grades thrift and harshness.
note.cn: 形近组把真正的同族词与两个只是词尾相同的词放在一起；近义组按节约与严酷的程度分级。

entries.definition: plain, severe, without comfort
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的；严峻的；同族形容词。

entries.definition: in a plain or severe manner
entries.definitionCN: 朴素地；严峻地；同族副词。

entries.definition: all future generations
entries.definitionCN: 后代；只是词尾音近，词源无关。

entries.definition: the state of being wealthy and successful

normalIntro.cn: austerity 是 austere 的名词：把「干涩」变成生活方式、风格与政策。

normal.en: The ending -ity turns an adjective into a quality.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ity 把形容词变成性质名词。

normal.en: Austerity measures is the fixed political phrase.
normal.cn: 紧缩措施是固定的政治搭配。

normal.en: The plural austerities means acts of self-denial.
normal.cn: 复数形式指一桩桩苦行。

normal.en: Austere describes things; austerity names the state.
normal.cn: 形容词描述事物，名词指那种状态。

normal.en: Prosperity only shares the ending, not the root.
normal.cn: 繁荣一词只是词尾相同，词根无关。

abstract.en: Picture a room from which every ornament is carried out.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，装饰被一件件搬走。

abstract.en: Picture a budget with whole lines crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一份预算，整行整行被划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a dry mouth that refuses the sweet wine.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干涩的嘴，拒绝那杯甜酒。

examples.en: Austerity shaped the design of the whole building.
examples.cn: 朴素的取向决定了整栋建筑的设计。

examples.en: The government imposed austerity after the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机之后政府推行了紧缩。

examples.en: The austerities of the monastery included silence at meals.
examples.cn: 修道院的苦行包括用餐时静默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「干涩」：把水分、装饰与享受都抽干，剩下的就是紧缩、清苦与严峻。

sensesIntro.en: Dryness becomes a policy, a way of life, a style, a face, a hard period and a spiritual discipline.
sensesIntro.cn: 「干涩」依次变成政策、生活方式、风格、面孔、艰苦时期与精神修行。

core.cn: 核心意象：装饰与舒适被一件件搬走，只剩必需

branches.en: a state cutting its spending

branches.en: a life without luxury

branches.en: a bare chapel wall
branches.cn: 光秃的小教堂墙面

branches.en: an unsmiling face
branches.cn: 不带笑意的面孔

branches.en: hard years and chosen discipline
branches.cn: 艰苦的岁月与自选的修行

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 austerus 与 austeritas 把希腊词干带进英语；更深的词根与「干燥」有关。

definition_zh: 监测；监控；监听；病情监测；环境监测；系统监控；项目进度跟踪；设备状态监测；监测体系
definition_en: the continuous watching, checking or recording of something over time in order to detect change, problems or progress
core_image: 一个人坐在一排屏幕前，眼睛在数值之间来回扫，一有异常就记下来
scene: 这里指「监测」。 A technician sits before a wall of screens, scanning the numbers for anything unusual: this watching is monitoring.
sceneCN: 这里 monitoring 是「监测」（第 1 个义项：持续观察并记录）；句意：一名技术员坐在一整面屏幕前，在数值间来回扫视，寻找任何异常，这种持续看护就是监测。图中可辨识物件：成排屏幕、跳动的曲线、值班员、记录本、警示灯。

forms.label: 名词（监测这一活动，不可数）

senses.title: Continuous watching and recording
senses.titleCN: 持续观察并记录：一直盯着看
senses.definition: the continuous watching and recording of a process over time in order to detect change
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内持续观察并记录某一过程，以便察觉变化
senses.example: Continuous monitoring of the river showed a slow rise in nitrates.
senses.exampleCN: 对河流的持续监测显示硝酸盐在缓慢上升。
senses.why: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds or warns', from monere 'to warn'. Monitoring is the work of that warner: it keeps watch so that a change can be announced before it becomes damage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 意为「提醒者、警告者」，出自 monere「警告」。monitoring 就是这位警告者的工作：它一直看着，好让变化在造成损害之前被报出来。

senses.title: Security surveillance: watching a place or person
senses.titleCN: 安防监控：看住一个场所或一个人
senses.definition: the watching of a place, building or person by cameras or guards for security
senses.definitionCN: 为安全目的用摄像头或人员看守某场所、建筑或某个人
senses.example: The station is under constant camera monitoring.
senses.exampleCN: 这个车站处于持续的摄像头监控之下。
senses.why: Here the warner is a camera rather than a voice. The word keeps its neutral sense of keeping watch, though the purpose shifts from warning to policing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的警告者是一台摄像头，而不是一个声音。词仍保持「看守」的中性义，只是目的从预警转向治安。

senses.title: Patient monitoring: tracking vital signs
senses.titleCN: 病情监测：盯住生命体征
senses.definition: the regular or continuous checking of a patient's condition, such as heart rate, blood pressure or oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 定期或持续检查病人状况，如心率、血压或血氧
senses.example: The nurses kept the patient under close monitoring overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 护士整夜对这名病人密切监护。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word for watching that can save a life. The monitor is the instrument and the nurse together, both standing between the patient and a sudden change.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个词指能够救命的看护。监测者既是仪器也是护士，两者都守在病人与突变之间。

senses.title: Environmental monitoring: checking air, water and soil
senses.titleCN: 环境监测：定期检查空气水土
senses.definition: the systematic measurement and recording of environmental conditions such as air quality, water chemistry or noise
senses.definitionCN: 对空气质量、水体化学成分或噪声等环境状况的系统测量与记录
senses.example: Environmental monitoring detected the leak within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 环境监测在数小时内就查出了泄漏。
senses.why: Pollution is invisible until it is measured. Monitoring turns the environment into a record that can be compared across seasons and used as evidence.
senses.whyCN: 污染在被测量之前是看不见的。监测把环境变成一份可跨季节比较、并可作为证据的记录。

senses.title: System monitoring: checking servers and networks
senses.titleCN: 系统监控：盯住服务器与网络
senses.definition: the automated checking of computer systems, networks or applications for faults and performance problems
senses.definitionCN: 对计算机系统、网络或应用自动进行检查，以发现故障与性能问题
senses.example: System monitoring alerted the team before the disk filled.
senses.exampleCN: 系统监控在磁盘写满之前就向团队发出警报。
senses.why: Software fails quietly, so something must watch it continuously. The old warner becomes a script that checks, alerts and records, with no human eye in the loop.
senses.whyCN: 软件会悄无声息地坏掉，因此必须有东西持续盯着。古老的「警告者」变成了检查、报警并记录的脚本，人眼不再需要一直在场。

senses.title: Tracking progress in education or a project
senses.titleCN: 进度跟踪：看学生或项目走到哪一步
senses.definition: the regular checking of a learner's or a project's progress against a plan
senses.definitionCN: 对照计划定期检查学习者或项目的进展
senses.example: Progress monitoring helps teachers adjust the pace.
senses.exampleCN: 进度跟踪帮助教师调整节奏。
senses.why: Here what is watched is movement through a plan rather than a machine's state. Monitoring makes progress visible early enough to change it.
senses.whyCN: 这里被盯住的是在计划中走了多远，而不是机器的状态。监测让进展早到足以被改变的时候被看见。

senses.title: Condition monitoring of equipment
senses.titleCN: 设备状态监测：听机器的异常征兆
senses.definition: the checking of machine condition, such as vibration, temperature or wear, in order to predict failure
senses.definitionCN: 检查机器的状况，如振动、温度或磨损，以预测故障
senses.example: Condition monitoring caught the bearing wear early.
senses.exampleCN: 状态监测很早就发现了轴承磨损。
senses.why: Engineering watches symptoms rather than outcomes. A bearing that runs hot is already speaking, and monitoring is the practice of listening in time.
senses.whyCN: 工程盯的是征兆而不是结果。发热的轴承已经在说话，而监测就是及时去听的那门功夫。

senses.title: A monitoring programme: the organised system
senses.titleCN: 监测体系：成体系的安排
senses.definition: an organised, long-term arrangement of instruments, schedules and reports for watching something
senses.definitionCN: 由仪器、时间表与报告组成的、长期有组织的观察安排
senses.example: The forest monitoring programme has run for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项森林监测计划已经运行了三十年。
senses.why: When monitoring lasts decades, it becomes an institution with staff, stations and archives. The activity noun then names the whole arrangement that keeps watch.
senses.whyCN: 当监测持续数十年，它就成了有人员、站点与档案的制度。这个活动名词于是指整套维持观察的安排。

intro.en: Monitoring is the English noun from monitor plus -ing. Monitor comes from Latin monitor 'one who reminds or warns', from monere 'to warn, advise'. English borrowed monitor in the 16th century for a person who advises or corrects, and extended it to instruments and then to continuous electronic watching in the 20th century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monitoring 是英语名词 monitor 加 -ing。monitor 出自拉丁语 monitor「提醒者、警告者」，源自 monere「警告、告诫」。英语在 16 世纪借入 monitor，指提出劝告或纠正的人，后扩展到仪器，20 世纪又扩展到持续的电子监视。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Electronic monitoring, patient monitoring and system monitoring become standard phrases as sensors spread.
items.cn: 随着传感器普及，electronic monitoring（电子监控）、patient monitoring（病人监护）、system monitoring（系统监控）成为固定说法。

items.en: Monitor extends from the person who warns to the instrument that displays or checks, such as a ship's monitor.
items.cn: monitor 从发出警告的人扩展到显示或检查的仪器，如船上的监测装置。

items.en: English monitor names a person who admonishes or keeps order, including the school monitor.
items.cn: 英语 monitor 指提出告诫或维持秩序的人，包括学校里的班长。

items.en: monitor is 'the one who reminds', built on monere 'to warn, advise', whose participle is monitus.
items.cn: monitor 是「提醒者」，建立在 monere「警告、告诫」上，其分词为 monitus。

items.en: monere is often traced to a reconstructed root *men- 'to think', which also gives mental and comment, though the link is generally accepted.
items.cn: monere 常被追溯到重构词根 *men-「思考」，该词根也给出 mental 与 comment，但这一联系一般认为成立。

note.en: The first group separates two genuine relatives and one false friend; the second compares words for watching that differ in purpose and openness.
note.cn: 第一组把两个真正的同族词与一个假朋友分开；第二组比较在目的与公开程度上不同的「看」类词。

entries.definition: to watch and check something, or a screen or person that does so. Monitoring is simply the ongoing activity of this verb.
entries.definitionCN: 监测、检查某物，或指做这事的屏幕或人。monitoring 只是这个动词的持续活动形式。

entries.definition: to warn or reprimand someone firmly. It is ad- 'to' plus monere, the same warning verb behind monitor, but it names the speech act rather than the watching.
entries.definitionCN: 严厉警告或责备某人。它是 ad-「向」加 monere，与 monitor 同出一个「警告」动词，但指言语行为而非观察。

entries.definition: relating to money. It comes from Latin moneta 'mint, coinage', not from monere, and only shares the opening letters.
entries.definitionCN: 与货币有关的。它出自拉丁语 moneta「铸币厂、钱币」，并非来自 monere，只是开头字母相同。

entries.definition: close watching of a person or place, often by authorities and often without consent. It carries suspicion that monitoring does not always imply.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或场所的密切注视，常由当局进行且常未经同意。它带有怀疑色彩，而 monitoring 未必有此含义。

entries.definition: the act of noticing something carefully. It may be a single act, where monitoring implies a sustained series of checks.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细注意某事的行为。它可以是一次性的，而 monitoring 暗示持续的一系列检查。

entries.definition: following the position or progress of something over time. It stresses the path, where monitoring stresses the state and the alert.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间跟踪某物的位置或进展。它强调轨迹，而 monitoring 强调状态与警报。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monere means 'to warn', so a monitor is a warner and monitoring is the act of staying awake on someone's behalf.
normal.cn: monere 意为「警告」，所以 monitor 是警告者，monitoring 则是替别人保持清醒的行为。

normal.en: admonish, admonition, summon and premonition all contain monere, the same warning verb.
normal.cn: admonish、admonition、summon、premonition 都含 monere，即同一个「警告」动词。

normal.en: monetary looks similar but comes from moneta 'mint'; money is not the same root as warning.
normal.cn: monetary 看着相似，却出自 moneta「铸币厂」；钱与警告不是同一个词根。

normal.en: The -ing form makes the verb into an activity, so monitoring names the ongoing watch rather than one check.
normal.cn: -ing 形式把动词变成活动，因此 monitoring 指持续的看守，而不是一次检查。

normal.en: Each field adds its object to the same activity: patient, environment, system, progress, condition.
normal.cn: 每个领域都是把各自的对象接到同一个活动上：病人、环境、系统、进度、状态。

abstract.en: Picture a night watchman who never sleeps because a script now does the rounds.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从不睡觉的更夫，因为如今是一段脚本在巡夜。

abstract.en: Monitoring is attention turned into a record: what is not written down cannot be compared later.
abstract.cn: 监测是把注意力变成记录：没被写下的东西，事后无法比较。

abstract.en: The word always implies that something could go wrong, and that someone wants to know first.
abstract.cn: 这个词总暗示：某事可能出错，而有人想先知道。

examples.en: Monitoring of the volcano began weeks before the eruption.
examples.cn: 对这座火山的监测在喷发前数周就开始了。

examples.en: The hospital uses remote monitoring for recovering patients.
examples.cn: 这家医院对康复期病人使用远程监护。

examples.en: Without monitoring, the restoration work could fail silently.
examples.cn: 没有监测，这项修复工作可能无声无息地失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸你特宁」——夜里摸一遍设备，特别宁静才算过关 → monitoring 监测、监控

root: 拉丁语 monere「警告、告诫」→ monitor「提醒者、警告者」→ 英语 monitor；加 -ing → monitoring。核心是「替别人一直盯着，一有不对就先说出来」。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: someone or something keeping watch over time. What changes is what is watched — a process, a place, a patient, the environment, a system, a learner, a machine, or a whole long-term programme.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：某人或某物在时间中持续看守。变化的只是看守的对象——一个过程、一处场所、一名病人、环境、一套系统、一名学习者、一台机器，还是整个长期计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a technician before a wall of screens, scanning for anything unusual.
core.cn: 核心意象：技术员坐在一整面屏幕前，扫视任何异常。

branches.en: THE WARNER: monere 'to warn' supplies the purpose, which is to notice change early enough to act.
branches.cn: 警告者：monere「警告」提供了目的，即早到足以采取行动地察觉变化。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PLACES: cameras watch a station, instruments and nurses watch a patient.
branches.cn: 人与场所：摄像头看守车站，仪器与护士看守病人。

branches.en: ENVIRONMENT AND MACHINES: air, water and bearings all give signs before they fail.
branches.cn: 环境与机器：空气、水和轴承在失效之前都会给出征兆。

branches.en: SOFTWARE: the watch is automated, and the alert arrives before the disk is full.
branches.cn: 软件：看守被自动化，警报在磁盘写满之前到达。

branches.en: PROGRESS AND PROGRAMMES: learners are checked against a plan, and decades of checking become an institution.
branches.cn: 进度与计划：学习者对照计划被检查，数十年的检查则成为一个制度。

intro.en: Monitoring is monitor plus -ing. The ending -ing turns the verb into a noun of activity; monitor is Latin monitor 'one who reminds', from monere 'to warn'.
intro.cn: monitoring 是 monitor 加 -ing。词尾 -ing 把动词变成活动名词；monitor 是拉丁语 monitor「提醒者」，出自 monere「警告」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is monere 'to warn, advise', with participle monitus. It also gives admonish, admonition, summon, premonition and monument.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词是 monere「警告、告诫」，分词为 monitus。它还给出 admonish、admonition、summon、premonition、monument。

items.meaning: the ongoing act of watching and checking
items.meaningCN: 持续观察与检查的活动
items.example: Monitoring revealed the first signs of change.
items.exampleCN: 监测揭示了变化的最初迹象。

items.meaning: to watch and check, or the device that does so
items.meaningCN: 监测；亦指监视器或监测者
items.exampleCN: 传感器每小时监测一次温度。

items.example: The monitored area is fenced off.
items.exampleCN: 受监测的区域被围了起来。

items.example: Unmonitored wells can run dry unnoticed.
items.exampleCN: 无人监测的水井可能干涸而无人察觉。

items.meaning: to warn or scold gently but firmly
items.example: The teacher admonished the class for lateness.
items.exampleCN: 老师因迟到告诫了全班。

items.meaning: a structure that reminds later generations
items.meaningCN: 纪念碑；纪念物（字面「提醒之物」）
items.example: The monument marks the old border.
items.exampleCN: 这座纪念碑标出旧边界。

items.meaning: to show clearly, and so to prove
items.meaningCN: 演示；证明（de- 表示彻底，monstrare 出自 monere）
items.example: The test demonstrates the effect clearly.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试清楚地展示了该效应。

items.meaningCN: 召唤；传唤（sub- 表示私下提醒）

items.example: She had a premonition of trouble.
