branches.cn: 隔绝以及与作物农场的界线。

intro.en: The ranch- family is small and Western: ranch, rancher and ranching all describe the same holding and the people who work it.
intro.cn: ranch 词族小而带西部味：ranch、rancher、ranching 都描述同一片土地与经营它的人。

latinIntro.en: Spanish rancho is the direct source; it probably goes back to a Latin word for a shared meal, which explains the early sense of a workers' hut.
latinIntro.cn: 西班牙语 rancho 是直接来源；它很可能回到拉丁语指共餐的词，这也解释了早先「工人棚屋」的意思。

items.exampleCN: 一位有经验的牧场工人。

definition_zh: 浓缩的；浓度高的；集中的；专心的；聚焦的
definition_en: made stronger or denser by removing water or spreading less widely, or brought to bear on one point
core_image: 一大锅清汤被小火慢慢收干，最后只剩一小碗味道极浓的汁
scene: 厨房里，厨师把一大锅汤小火收干，最后盛出一小碗味道极浓的汁。 The cook concentrated the broth until one cup held the flavour of the whole pot.
sceneCN: 这里 concentrated 指去掉水分使浓度提高（第 1 个义项：浓缩的）；句意为厨师把汤收干，直到一杯汁含有一整锅的味道。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、炉火、小碗、汤勺。

derivatives.zh: 同心的（同出 center 词根）

senses.title: Made denser by removing water
senses.definition: reduced in volume by removing water or another liquid so that the remaining substance is stronger
senses.definitionCN: 通过除去水或其他液体而缩小体积，使剩余部分更浓
senses.example: The concentrated syrup is diluted before bottling.
senses.exampleCN: 浓缩糖浆在装瓶前会被稀释。
senses.why: concentrated is the participle of concentrate, from con- 'together' plus centrum 'center', so the parts are driven toward one center and the volume shrinks.
senses.whyCN: concentrated 是 concentrate 的分词，来自 con-「共同」加 centrum「中心」，即把各部分赶向一个中心，体积随之缩小。

senses.title: Containing a high proportion of the active substance
senses.titleCN: 有效成分含量高的、浓烈的
senses.definition: having a large amount of an active ingredient in a small volume, so that a little does a great deal
senses.definitionCN: 小体积内含大量有效成分，一点点就能起很大作用
senses.example: A drop of concentrated acid burned the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴浓酸把实验台烧出了痕。
senses.why: once the water is removed, the active part makes up most of what is left, which is the measurable form of the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 水分去掉后，有效部分占了剩下的大部分，这是第一义的可测量形式。

senses.title: Gathered into one area
senses.definition: existing mainly in one place rather than spread out over a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 主要存在于一处，而非分散在广阔区域
senses.example: Industry remained concentrated in three coastal cities.
senses.exampleCN: 工业仍集中在三座沿海城市。
senses.why: the same movement toward a center applies to people and factories, so concentration becomes a matter of geography.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「向中心靠拢」的运动也适用于人与工厂，于是集中成了地理问题。

senses.title: Held in few hands
senses.titleCN: 权力或资源集中在少数人手中
senses.definition: gathered into a small number of hands or institutions rather than widely shared
senses.definitionCN: 被收拢到少数人或不多的机构手中，而非广泛分享
senses.example: Concentrated power made the board hard to challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 集中的权力使董事会难以被挑战。
senses.why: power that is brought to one center can act as a single force, which is why concentration is also a political word.
senses.whyCN: 被收拢到一个中心的权力能作为单一力量行动，因此 concentration 也是政治词汇。

senses.title: Fully focused in attention
senses.definition: carried out with attention fixed on one task, with distractions shut out
senses.definitionCN: 注意力固定在一件事上、排除干扰地进行
senses.example: A concentrated effort finished the report in one evening.
senses.exampleCN: 一次专注的努力在一个晚上完成了报告。
senses.why: the mind is told to gather itself to one center, so concentration becomes the everyday word for attention.
senses.whyCN: 头脑被要求向一个中心聚拢，于是 concentration 成了「专注」的日常说法。

senses.title: Brought into a narrow beam
senses.definition: directed into a narrow beam or small area so that its effect is stronger
senses.definitionCN: 被导入狭窄光束或小范围，使效果更强
senses.example: The lens produced a concentrated beam of light.
senses.exampleCN: 透镜产生了一束聚焦的光。
senses.why: light obeys the same geometry as anything else gathered to a point, so optics uses the participle literally.
senses.whyCN: 光遵守与一切向一点聚拢之物相同的几何，因此光学直接使用这个分词。

senses.title: Fixed on a single object
senses.titleCN: 注意力落在某一对象上
senses.definition: directed toward one particular thing, often followed by on, as attention or study is
senses.definitionCN: 朝向某一个特定事物，常后接表示关涉的介词，如注意力或研究
senses.example: Her attention was concentrated on the single page.
senses.exampleCN: 她的注意力全落在那一页上。
senses.why: concentration needs an object, and the participle with on names the point at which the gathering arrives.
senses.whyCN: 集中总要有对象，带关涉介词的分词就点明聚拢所抵达的那一点。

senses.title: Collected into one strong whole
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：分散之物被收成一束
senses.definition: used figuratively of scattered material, effort or argument gathered into one forceful whole
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指零散的材料、努力或论证被收拢成一个有力的整体
senses.example: Ten years of scattered notes became one concentrated argument.
senses.exampleCN: 十年零散的笔记变成一个高度凝练的论证。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the geometry but drops the liquid: what is gathered is meaning rather than matter.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了这一几何关系却去掉了液体：被收拢的是意义，而非物质。

intro.en: Concentrated is the past participle of concentrate, from con- 'together' plus Late Latin centrare 'to center', itself from centrum 'center', from Greek kentron 'sharp point, goad'. The chemical sense of reducing volume dates from the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: concentrated 是 concentrate 的过去分词，来自 con-「共同」加晚期拉丁 centrare「置于中心」，后者出自 centrum「中心」，再上溯希腊 kentron「尖点、刺棒」。缩减体积的化学义始于十七世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kentron named a sharp point, a goad and the fixed point of a pair of compasses, and Greek geometry used it for the center of a circle.
items.cn: kentron 指尖点、刺棒，也指圆规固定的那一点，希腊几何用它表示圆心。

items.en: Latin took kentron as centrum 'center', the middle point from which distances are measured.
items.cn: 拉丁把 kentron 借作 centrum「中心」，即测量距离时所依据的中点。

items.en: Con- 'together' plus centrare produced concentrare 'to bring to a common center, to press together'.
items.cn: con-「共同」加 centrare 构成 concentrare「使聚到同一中心、压紧」。

items.en: Seventeenth-century chemistry used the participle for liquids reduced by evaporation, so that a small volume carried the strength of a large one.
items.cn: 十七世纪化学用这个分词指经蒸发缩减的液体，使小体积承载大体积的强度。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the same participle described attention, power and population gathered to one point rather than spread out.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，同一分词用来描述注意力、权力与人口被收拢到一点而非散布开来。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek origin of kentron is unsettled, and any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：kentron 在希腊语之前的来源没有定论，为其提出的更古老词根属于重构形式，而非已证实的形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the center root, which look alike but point in different directions; group two holds adjectives for things packed tightly together.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「中心」词根、形近而方向不同的词；第二组是形容紧密聚在一起的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb 'to bring to a center': to focus attention or to reduce a liquid by removing water.
entries.definitionCN: 「聚向中心」的动词：集中注意力，或除去水分使液体变浓。

entries.definition: Describes circles that share one center; it is about geometry, not about strength or attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容共用同一个圆心的圆；说的是几何，不是强度或注意力。

entries.definition: Ec- 'out of' plus centrum: off center, hence odd or unconventional in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: ec-「离开」加 centrum：偏离中心，因此指行为古怪、不合常规。

entries.definition: The middle point itself; every prefixed form is read against this plain noun.
entries.definitionCN: 中点本身；每个带前缀的形式都要对照这个朴素名词来读。

entries.definition: Having parts packed closely together; a dense fog is not necessarily a concentrated solution.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分紧密挤压；浓雾未必是浓溶液。

entries.definition: Very strong in degree, used of light, feeling or activity rather than of a measured solution.
entries.definitionCN: 程度极强，用于光、情感或活动，而非可测量的溶液。

entries.definition: Made shorter or thicker, as condensed milk or a condensed report; it stresses compression rather than a center.
entries.definitionCN: 被缩短或变稠，如炼乳或摘要；强调压缩，而非中心。

entries.definition: Brought to a point of attention or a point of light; it rarely carries the chemical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被收拢到注意力或光的某一点；很少带化学义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Con- 'together' plus centrum 'center': everything is driven to one point.
normal.cn: con-「共同」加 centrum「中心」：一切都被赶向一点。

normal.en: The family runs concentrate, concentration, concentrated, concentric, eccentric.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 concentrate、concentration、concentrated、concentric、eccentric。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: concentrated juice, concentrated power, concentrated effort.
normal.cn: 固定搭配切分义项：浓缩果汁、集中的权力、专注的努力。

normal.en: The chemical sense pairs with dilute: concentrated acid against dilute acid.
normal.cn: 化学义与 dilute 配对：浓酸对稀酸。

normal.en: The adjective keeps the participle ending -ed, so it describes a result already achieved.
normal.cn: 这个形容词保留分词词尾 -ed，因此描述已经完成的结果。

abstract.en: Picture a whole orchard boiled down into one spoonful of jam.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片果园被熬成一勺果酱。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred voices at last singing the same note.
abstract.cn: 想象一百个声音终于唱在同一个音上。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp behind one small hole, lighting a single spot on a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象灯后只留一个小孔，把光打墙上的一点。

examples.en: The factory ships concentrated orange juice and adds water at the other end.
examples.cn: 工厂运出浓缩橙汁，到另一端再加水。

examples.en: Rainfall is concentrated in two months, so the fields need irrigation later.
examples.cn: 降雨集中在两个月里，因此田里之后需要灌溉。

examples.en: The final hour of study was more concentrated than the whole afternoon before it.
examples.cn: 最后一小时的学习比之前整个下午都更专注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ centr（中心）+ ated」——全往一个中心挤：浓缩的、集中的、专注的

root: 拉丁 concentrare「聚到同一中心、压紧」的过去分词 concentratus = con-（共同）+ centrum（中心）；centrum 出自希腊 kentron（尖点），其更早来源不确定。英语 concentrate 的过去分词作形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gathering to a center: water leaves and a liquid grows strong, the active part dominates, factories and people cluster, power collects in few hands, attention fixes on a task, light is narrowed to a beam, attention lands on one object, and finally scattered meaning is pressed into one argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「向中心聚拢」：水离开、液体变浓，有效成分占主导，工厂与人聚集，权力收进少数手中，注意力固定在一件事上，光被收成光束，注意力落在某一对象上，最后零散的意义被压成一个论证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large pot of thin broth reduced by slow heat until one small bowl holds all of its taste.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大锅清汤被小火收干，直到一小碗盛下全部味道。

branches.en: STRONGER LIQUID: removing water and raising the active share are the same reduction seen as process and as result.
branches.cn: 更浓的液体：去掉水与提高有效成分占比，是同一次缩减的过程与结果。

branches.en: GATHERED IN SPACE AND IN POWER: factories cluster and authority collects by the same centering movement.
branches.cn: 在空间与权力中聚拢：工厂聚集与权力收拢，是同一种向心运动。

branches.en: FIXED ATTENTION: the mind gathers itself and then lands on one named object.
branches.cn: 固定的注意力：头脑先聚拢自身，再落在某个被点明的对象上。

branches.en: NARROW BEAM: optics uses the same geometry to make light act at one spot.
branches.cn: 收窄的光束：光学用同一几何让光在一点上起作用。

branches.en: PRESSED MEANING: what is concentrated at the end is not matter but argument.
branches.cn: 被压紧的意义：最后被浓缩的不再是物质，而是论证。

intro.en: Concentrated is a prefixed Latin participle, and both the prefix and the center root build a large family of English words.
intro.cn: concentrated 是一个带前缀的拉丁分词，前缀与「中心」词根共同构成一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Con- 'together' plus centrum 'center' gives concentrate, concentration and concentric; ec- 'out of' gives eccentric, the word that moves the other way.
latinIntro.cn: con-「共同」加 centrum「中心」构成 concentrate、concentration 与 concentric；ec-「离开」构成 eccentric，即朝反方向移动的词。

items.example: The prefix gathers the parts toward one point.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把各部分聚向一点。

items.example: The noun supplies the point everything is gathered to.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供一切聚拢所向的那一点。

items.example: The Latin verb begins the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词开启整个词族。

items.example: The plant concentrates the juice by evaporation.
items.exampleCN: 工厂用蒸发使果汁变浓。

items.example: The concentrated acid is handled with gloves.

items.meaning: the act or state of being concentrated
items.example: The concentration of the solution was measured twice.
items.exampleCN: 溶液的浓度被测量了两次。

items.example: The concentrator removed half the water.
items.exampleCN: 浓缩器去掉了半数水分。

items.example: The reform deconcentrated authority to the regions.
items.exampleCN: 改革把权力下放到各地区。

latinEntries.meaning: to bring to a common center

definition_zh: 电容器
definition_en: a device that stores electric charge and energy in an electric field between conductive plates
core_image: 两片金属板隔着一层绝缘膜对峙：电荷挤在两边蓄势待发
scene: 拆开的旧收音机主板暴露在台灯下，各色元件密密麻麻。 A swollen capacitor had leaked and killed the radio.
sceneCN: 这里 capacitor 是「电容器」（第 1 个义项：储存电荷的元件）；句意是一只鼓包的电容器漏液，毁掉了收音机。

derivatives.zh: 同根专业名词，义为「电容（量）」
同根基础名词，义为「容量；能力」
由 capacitance 加形容词后缀构成，义为「电容的；电容性的」

senses.title: The charge-storing component
senses.definition: an electrical component of conductive plates separated by an insulator, storing charge and releasing it quickly
senses.definitionCN: 由绝缘层隔开的导电极板构成的电子元件，可储存并快速释放电荷
senses.example: The capacitor stores energy for the camera flash.
senses.exampleCN: 电容器为相机闪光灯储能。
senses.why: The device is named for what it does: it has great capacity to hold charge.
senses.whyCN: 器件因功能得名：它拥有储存电荷的巨大「容量」。

senses.title: The capacitor as circuit element
senses.definition: in circuit theory, the idealized element that opposes sudden voltage change and blocks direct current
senses.definitionCN: 电路理论中抵抗电压突变的理想化元件，可隔断直流
senses.example: Couple the two stages with a capacitor to block the DC offset.
senses.exampleCN: 用一只电容把两级电路耦合起来，隔掉直流偏置。
senses.why: Beyond the physical part, the word names the mathematical role in analysis.
senses.whyCN: 超出实物之外，这个词还指分析中对应的数学角色。

intro.en: Capacitor is a modern coinage on the Latin stem cap-, to hold, naming a device whose whole job is holding charge.
intro.cn: capacitor 是在拉丁词干 cap-（容纳）上的现代造词，命名一个专职「容纳电荷」的器件。

items.en: The root *kap- means to grasp or hold, the ancient base of have and heavy.
items.cn: 词根 *kap- 意为抓住、握有，是 have、heavy 等词的古老源头。

items.en: Latin capere meant to take or hold; capax described a thing able to hold much.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为拿取、容纳；capax 形容能装很多东西之物。

items.en: Early experimenters spoke of electrical capacity as bodies held charge; capacitance later quantified it.
items.cn: 十八世纪的实验者以「电容本领」描述物体储电；capacitance 一词后来将其定量化。

items.en: The device name capacitor, favored in American usage over condenser, spread with the electronics industry.
items.cn: 二十世纪，美式用法偏爱的 capacitor 随电子工业普及，取代了 condenser。

items.en: Today capacitors appear in everything from flash units to power grids and touchscreens.
items.cn: 如今电容器出现在闪光灯、电网到触控屏的一切设备中。

note.en: Capacitor belongs to the cap- holding family and carries one famous look-alike trap.
note.cn: capacitor 属于 cap-「容纳」词族，并带着一个著名的形近陷阱。

entries.definition: The measure of how much charge a capacitor can store per volt.
entries.definitionCN: 电容量，即电容器每伏特能储存的电荷量。

entries.definition: The amount something can hold or produce.
entries.definitionCN: 容量；产能；能力。

entries.definition: The component that resists current, the other basic passive part.
entries.definitionCN: 电阻器，抵抗电流的另一基本无源元件。

entries.definition: The older British name for a capacitor, still used for special types.
entries.definitionCN: 电容器旧称（英式），某些类型至今沿用。

entries.definition: A chemical energy store that releases charge slowly and steadily.
entries.definitionCN: 化学储能装置，缓慢稳定地释放电荷，与电容快速释放相对。

entries.definition: A charge-storing cell, older engineering vocabulary.
entries.definitionCN: 蓄电池；蓄能器，较老的工程用语。

entries.definition: The insulating layer between a capacitor's plates.
entries.definitionCN: 电容器极板间的绝缘介质层。

entries.definition: The component that stores energy in a magnetic field, the capacitor's dual.
entries.definitionCN: 电感器，在磁场中储能，是电容器的对偶元件。

entries.definition: A material that blocks charge flow, the middle layer's job.
entries.definitionCN: 绝缘体，阻挡电荷流动，即中间层的职责。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the hold root and the two-plate standoff.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「容纳」词根与「两板对峙」画面的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root core: capacitor holds charge, exactly as capacity holds amounts.
normal.cn: 词根核心：capacitor 容纳电荷，正如 capacity 容纳数量。

normal.en: Picture rule: two plates, one gap, charge pressed against both faces.
normal.cn: 画面规则：两块极板、一道缝隙，电荷紧压在两面上。

normal.en: Family row: capacity, capacitance, capacitor, capacitive climb the same stem.
normal.cn: 家族队列：capacity、capacitance、capacitor、capacitive 沿同一词干逐级而上。

normal.en: Usage split: American engineers say capacitor; British tradition long said condenser.
normal.cn: 用法分野：美国工程师说 capacitor，英国传统长期说 condenser。

normal.en: Function hook: it blocks DC but passes AC, the exam line worth memorizing.
normal.cn: 功能钩子：隔直流、通交流，是值得背下的考点句。

abstract.en: Two armies of charge glaring across a valley neither may cross, strength growing with the silence.
abstract.cn: 两军电荷隔着一条谁也过不去的峡谷对峙，沉默中力量不断积蓄。

abstract.en: A dam holding back a thin sheet of lightning, released in one blinding blink.
abstract.cn: 一道薄如蝉翼的闪电被水坝拦住，眨眼间倾泻而出。

abstract.en: A sandwich of metal, plastic, metal, thin enough to hide inside every gadget.
abstract.cn: 金属-塑料-金属的三明治，薄得能藏进任何小玩意。

examples.en: Technicians replaced every aging capacitor on the power board.
examples.cn: 技术人员更换了电源板上所有老化的电容器。

examples.en: The defibrillator's capacitor stores the charge for the life-saving jolt.
examples.cn: 除颤仪的电容器为救命的一击储存电荷。

examples.en: Touchscreens sense fingers through a grid of transparent capacitors.
examples.cn: 触控屏通过透明电容阵列感知手指。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克拍sitter」——「可拍」的照片全靠闪光灯，闪光灯里坐着（sitter）一只储电的电容；联想两块极板面对面「坐着」存电荷，即是电容器。

root: 现代科技造词，基于拉丁词干 cap-（容纳），出自 capere（拿取、容纳），可上溯至印欧词根 *kap-（抓取）。器件义为「储存电荷之物」，与 capacity（容量）、capacitance（电容量）、capacitive（电容性的）同族。美式英语用 capacitor，英式旧称 condenser。

sensesIntro.en: From the physical part the word extends to the idealized element of circuit theory.
sensesIntro.cn: 从实物元件出发，词义延伸到电路理论中的理想化元件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two charged plates separated by an insulator, energy held on a hair trigger.
core.cn: 核心意象：被绝缘层隔开的两块带电极板，能量蓄势于毫厘之间。

branches.en: THE BENCH: physical capacitors soldered into every board.
branches.cn: 工作台：焊进每块电路板的实物电容。

branches.en: THE EQUATION: the abstract element in analysis and design.
branches.cn: 方程：分析设计中的抽象元件。

branches.en: THE TIMING: capacitors set the heartbeat of circuits.
branches.cn: 节律：电容器设定电路的心跳。

branches.en: THE POWER GRID: capacitor banks steadying voltage.
branches.cn: 电网：稳定电压的电容器组。

branches.en: THE NAMESAKE: all of it named for the simple act of holding.
branches.cn: 词源呼应：这一切都因「容纳」这一朴素动作而得名。

intro.en: Capacitor is the Latin stem capac- plus the agent noun ending -or, the thing that holds.
intro.cn: capacitor 由拉丁词干 capac- 加施动名词词尾 -or 构成，即「容纳之器」。

latinIntro.en: The cap- stem of holding powers both everyday and technical vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: cap-「容纳」词干同时驱动日常与技术词汇。

definition_zh: 加剧；使恶化；激化（病情、问题、情绪）
definition_en: to make a bad situation, an illness or a feeling more severe
core_image: 原本只剩一点火星的炭堆被风一吹，火舌立刻窜高，把旁边的干草也点着
scene: 医生提醒病人，熬夜和饮酒会让本来稳定的病情明显加重。 Late nights and alcohol exacerbate the patient's condition.
sceneCN: 这里指让病情变得更严重（第 2 个义项：使疾病或症状加重）；句意：熬夜和饮酒会加重这位病人的病情。

senses.title: To make a problem worse
senses.definition: to increase the seriousness of a difficulty that is already present
senses.definitionCN: 使已经存在的困难变得更加严重
senses.example: The new tax exacerbated the shortage of housing.
senses.exampleCN: 新税加剧了住房短缺。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to make harsher, and a problem made harsher is a problem made worse.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为使更严酷，问题变严酷就是变严重。

senses.title: To aggravate an illness
senses.definition: to make a disease, a symptom or a condition more severe
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、症状或身体状况更加严重
senses.example: Late nights and alcohol exacerbate the patient's condition.
senses.exampleCN: 熬夜和饮酒会加重这位病人的病情。
senses.why: Medicine adopted the word because a harsh course of illness is exactly what the verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 医学采用这个词，因为病程变得凶险正是这个动词所描述的。

senses.title: To intensify a conflict
senses.definition: to make a dispute or a tension sharper and harder to settle
senses.definitionCN: 使争端或紧张局面更尖锐、更难平息
senses.example: The patrol exacerbated tensions along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 这次巡逻激化了边境的紧张局势。
senses.why: A conflict that grows sharper has taken on the bitterness the Latin adjective names.
senses.whyCN: 冲突变得更尖锐，正是染上了那个拉丁形容词所指的苦涩。

senses.title: To worsen economic conditions
senses.definition: to make an economic situation more difficult or unstable
senses.definitionCN: 使经济形势更困难或更不稳定
senses.example: A sudden rise in fuel costs exacerbated the slowdown.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料成本骤升加剧了经济放缓。
senses.why: An economy already slowing is a bad state, and the verb adds severity to something that exists.
senses.whyCN: 已经放缓的经济本就是坏状态，这个动词给已有之事再加上一层严重。

senses.title: To inflame a person's feelings
senses.definition: to make anger, grief or fear stronger and less controlled
senses.definitionCN: 使愤怒、悲伤或恐惧更强烈、更难控制
senses.example: The rumour exacerbated the crowd's anger.
senses.exampleCN: 这则传言使人群的愤怒更加激烈。
senses.why: The oldest English use was about irritated feeling, before the medical sense became dominant.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的用法就是被激怒的情绪，早于医学义成为主流。

senses.title: To worsen environmental damage
senses.definition: to increase the harm done to air, water, soil or living systems
senses.definitionCN: 加重对空气、水、土壤或生命系统的损害
senses.example: Draining the wetland exacerbated the loss of species.
senses.exampleCN: 排干湿地加剧了物种的消失。
senses.why: Environmental harm is an existing bad process, and any added pressure is an exacerbation of it.
senses.whyCN: 环境损害是一个已经存在的坏过程，任何外加压力都是对它的加剧。

senses.title: To make an injury or pain worse
senses.definition: to increase the severity of a wound or of physical pain
senses.definitionCN: 使伤口或身体的疼痛更加严重
senses.example: Walking on the ankle too soon exacerbated the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 脚踝过早承重使伤势加重。
senses.why: A wound is the most physical case, and the verb keeps the body in view even when the object is abstract.
senses.whyCN: 伤口是最物理的情形，即使宾语抽象，这个动词仍保留身体的画面。

senses.title: To deepen inequality or disadvantage
senses.titleCN: 加剧不平等或弱势处境
senses.definition: to make an existing gap in wealth, access or opportunity wider
senses.definitionCN: 使财富、机会或获取途径上已有的差距更大
senses.example: The fee structure exacerbated the gap between rich and poor schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这套收费结构加剧了富裕学校与贫困学校之间的差距。
senses.why: A gap is imagined as a cut in a surface, and making it deeper is the same picture as making a problem worse.
senses.whyCN: 差距被想象成表面的一道切口，把它弄得更深与把问题弄得更糟是同一幅画。

intro.en: Exacerbate comes from a Latin verb meaning to make harsher, built on an adjective for bitter and severe. English took it in the fifteenth century through French, and medicine gave it its modern prominence.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示使更严酷的拉丁动词，其基础是一个表示苦涩与严酷的形容词。英语在十五世纪经法语借入，医学给了它今天的显著地位。

items.en: Acer meant sharp, keen or fierce, and it stands behind words for sourness and for sharpness of temper.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词意为尖锐、强烈、猛烈，英语中表示酸味与脾气尖刻的词都出自它。

items.en: Acerbus meant bitter, harsh and unripe, and it described both taste and manner.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词意为苦涩、严酷、未成熟，既描述味道，也描述态度。

items.en: The prefix meant out or thoroughly, and here it intensified the harshness.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示向外或彻底，在这里加强了严酷的程度。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to make bitter or harsh, and to irritate or provoke.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为使苦涩、使严酷，也指激怒、刺激。

items.en: English took the verb through French in the fifteenth century, first for irritated feelings.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪经法语借入，先用于被激怒的情绪。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine made the verb the standard word for a disease growing worse.
items.cn: 十九世纪的医学使这个动词成为表示病情加重的标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares the bitter root or its English relatives; the second group names nearby ways of making something worse. Exacerbate always makes an existing bad thing worse, while counteract pushes back against an effect, so the two point in opposite directions.
note.cn: 第一组共享苦涩词根或其英语亲属；第二组是相邻的使坏加重的说法。本词总是让已经不好的事更糟，对抗类词则朝效应回推，两者方向相反。

entries.definition: A sharpening of a disease or of a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病或问题的急剧加重。

entries.definition: Sharp and bitter in speech; it describes the manner, not the worsening.
entries.definitionCN: 言辞尖刻苦涩；描述态度，而非加重过程。

entries.definition: Bitterness in relations, which is what exacerbation often produces.
entries.definitionCN: 关系中的尖刻敌意，常是加剧之后的结果。

entries.definition: Sharp and unpleasant to smell or taste; the sensory relative of bitter.
entries.definitionCN: 刺鼻难闻的；是苦涩在感官上的亲属。

entries.definition: To become or make worse; it is the plain word without the sense of sharpening.
entries.definitionCN: 变坏或使变坏；是平实说法，不含「变尖锐」之意。

entries.definition: To make worse, especially an illness or an offence; it is close but often stronger in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 使更严重，尤指病情或过失；意思接近，医学中常用得更重。

entries.definition: To make stronger; it need not be bad, since intensity can be neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 使更强；不一定坏，因为强度可以是中性的。

entries.definition: To stir up strong feeling or to make a body part red and sore.
entries.definitionCN: 激起强烈情绪，或使身体部位红肿疼痛。

entries.definition: To raise the degree of something; it can be neutral or positive.
entries.definitionCN: 提高某种程度；可为中性或正面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the bitter root, the real family and the objects that show what can be made worse.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用苦涩词根、真实同族词，以及能显示可使恶化之对象的搭配。

normal.en: The root means bitter, so the verb means to make a thing more bitter than it already was.
normal.cn: 词根意为苦涩，动词就是让本来苦涩的事更加苦涩。

normal.en: The family runs exacerbation, exacerbating, exacerbated and the related adjective acerbic.
normal.cn: 同族词有加重、使恶化的、被加重的，以及同根的「尖刻」形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: exacerbate a problem, exacerbate symptoms, exacerbate tensions.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：使问题恶化、加重症状、激化紧张局势。

normal.en: Medicine is its strongest home: a disease that grows sharper is the standard case.
normal.cn: 医学是它最主要的归宿：病程变得凶险是标准情形。

normal.en: It never means to create a problem, only to make an existing one worse.
normal.cn: 它从不表示制造问题，只表示让已有的问题更严重。

abstract.en: Picture a small flame fanned by a sudden wind until it catches the dry grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一点小火被突来的风一吹，烧着了干草。

abstract.en: Picture a crack in a wall widened by one hard frost.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一道裂缝被一场严霜撑得更宽。

abstract.en: Picture an angry word that makes a whole room angrier.
abstract.cn: 想象一句愤怒的话让满屋的人更愤怒。

examples.en: Cutting the budget would exacerbate the staffing problem.
examples.cn: 削减预算会使人员问题更加严重。

examples.en: Cold air can exacerbate a lung condition.
examples.cn: 冷空气可能加重肺部疾病。

examples.en: The delay exacerbated the dispute between the two sides.
examples.cn: 这次拖延激化了双方的争端。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊格」加「扎瑟贝特」——往苦药里再加一把苦艾，病更难受：加剧、恶化

root: 拉丁语「尖锐」衍生出「苦涩、严酷」的形容词，加表示彻底的强意前缀构成「使更严酷」，十五世纪经法语进入英语，十九世纪在医学中定型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all sharpen something already bad: a problem, an illness, a conflict, an economy, a feeling, the environment, an injury and an inequality.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把已经不好的事变得更尖锐：问题、疾病、冲突、经济、情绪、环境、伤势与不平等。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of embers fanned by a sudden gust, flames leaping up and catching the dry grass beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本只剩一点火星的炭堆被风一吹，火舌立刻窜高，把旁边的干草也点着。

branches.en: THE PROBLEM: a difficulty made worse, and an economy pushed further down.
branches.cn: 问题：变得更严重的困难，以及被进一步压下去的经济。

branches.en: THE BODY: a disease aggravated and an injury made more painful.
branches.cn: 身体：被加重的疾病与被弄得更痛的伤势。

branches.en: THE CONFLICT AND THE FEELING: sharper tensions and angrier emotions.
branches.cn: 冲突与情绪：更尖锐的紧张局势与更激烈的情绪。

branches.en: THE ENVIRONMENT: harm to water, air and living systems increased.
branches.cn: 环境：对水、空气与生命系统的损害被加重。

branches.en: THE GAP: inequality between groups made wider.
branches.cn: 差距：群体之间的不平等被拉大。

intro.en: Exacerbate is a Latin verb of bitterness and severity, and its family supplies the noun of worsening and adjectives for the sharp manner behind it.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示苦涩与严酷的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示恶化的名词，以及描述其背后尖刻态度的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin acer and acerbus supply the bitter core, and the prefix ex- supplies the intensifying push.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示尖锐与苦涩的两个形容词提供苦涩核心，前缀提供加强的推力。

items.example: It intensifies the harshness of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它加强那个形容词的严酷程度。

items.example: The root supplies the edge of the meaning.
The adjective supplies the taste and the manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供味道与态度。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the Latin stem an English verb shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给拉丁词干披上英语动词外形。

items.example: It builds the medical noun for a sharp turn for the worse.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示病情急剧转坏的名词。

items.example: It builds the participle and the adjective.
It marks a condition already made worse.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已经被加重的状况。

items.example: It builds the related adjective for bitter speech.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示言语尖刻的同根形容词。
